definition_zh: 成功地；顺利地
definition_en: in a way that achieves the result you wanted
core_image: 穿过最后一道门，门上的灯变绿
scene: 她成功地修复了那台旧钟。 She successfully repaired the old clock.
sceneCN: 这里 successfully 是「成功地」（第 1 个义项）；句意：她成功地修复了那台旧钟。

senses.title: With success
senses.definition: in a way that achieves the wanted result
senses.definitionCN: 以达成预期结果的方式
senses.example: She successfully applied for the job.
senses.exampleCN: 她成功申请到了那份工作。
senses.why: This is the core sense of doing something well.
senses.whyCN: 这是把事情做成的核心义项。

senses.title: Without failure
senses.definition: without problems or failure
senses.definitionCN: 没有出现问题或失败
senses.example: The operation was successfully completed.
senses.exampleCN: 手术顺利完成。
senses.why: Here the point is that nothing went wrong.
senses.whyCN: 这里强调过程没有出差错。

intro.en: Successfully is success with two endings added one after another.
intro.cn: successfully 是 success 接连加上两个后缀构成的。

items.en: Cedere meant to go or to give way.

items.en: Successus meant a good outcome.

items.cn: success 意为好结果。

items.en: Success gained the ending -ful.
items.cn: success 加上了后缀 -ful。

items.en: The adverb ending -ly then formed successfully.
items.cn: 再加上副词后缀 -ly，形成了 successfully。

note.en: Successfully is compared with look-alike words and with words for smooth action.
note.cn: 把 successfully 与形近词以及表示顺利行事的词作比较。

abstract.en: To act successfully is to leave fewer problems than you found.
abstract.cn: 成功行事，就是让问题比来时更少。

abstract.en: Successfully does not mean easily.

abstract.en: The quietest work is often done most successfully.
abstract.cn: 最安静的工作，往往做得最成功。

definition_zh: 支配；控制；占首要地位；高耸于
definition_en: to have power over someone or something, to be the most important feature, or to stand above a place
core_image: 一座塔的影子慢慢铺满整条街道
scene: 半山腰那座塔的影子每天准时铺满整个村子。 A single tower dominates the skyline of the old town.
sceneCN: 这里 dominate 是「高耸于、俯瞰」（第 3 个义项：在某处上方高高立起并成为最显眼的景象）；句意是一座孤塔高耸于老城的天际线。

pos.zh: 动词：支配；控制；占首要地位；高耸于

senses.title: To control people or places
senses.definition: to have power and influence over a person, group, market or place
senses.definitionCN: 对某人、某群体、市场或地方拥有权力与影响
senses.example: A few large firms dominate the shipping industry.
senses.exampleCN: 几家大公司支配着航运业。
senses.why: The verb comes from dominari, to rule as a master of the house, so dominating is making others live under your direction.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词来自 dominari，即以一家之主的身份统治；所以 dominate 就是让别人在你的指挥下行事。

senses.title: To be the main feature
senses.definition: to be the most important, noticeable or frequent part of something
senses.definitionCN: 成为某事物中最重要、最显眼或出现最多的部分
senses.example: Talk of the storm dominated the evening news.
senses.exampleCN: 有关风暴的消息占据了当晚新闻的主要部分。
senses.why: Whatever occupies the largest share behaves like the master of a room: it sets the tone for everything else.
senses.whyCN: 占据最大份额的东西就像屋子的主人，别的都要跟着它定调。

senses.title: To tower above a place
senses.definition: to stand high above a place and be seen from all around it
senses.definitionCN: 在某处高高立起，从四周都能看见
senses.example: The cathedral dominates the square below it.
senses.exampleCN: 大教堂高耸于它下方的广场之上。
senses.why: A tower that fills the view from every street acts like a master overlooking a household, so the verb extends to height.
senses.whyCN: 从每条街望过去都占满视野的塔，就像俯视家户的主人，于是这个动词又扩展到高度。

intro.en: Dominate is the English verb built on Latin dominari, to rule, and on dominus, master of a household.
intro.cn: dominate 是英语动词，建立在拉丁语 dominari（统治）与 dominus（一家之主）之上。

items.en: Domus, house or household, is the oldest word in the family.
items.cn: domus（房子、家户）是这一族里最古老的词。

items.en: Dominus named the master of the household and later any lord or owner.
items.cn: dominus 指一家之主，后来泛指主人或所有者。

items.en: Dominari meant to rule, to exercise mastery over people or things.
items.cn: dominari 意为统治，对人施加支配。

items.en: The participle dominatus described something ruled or controlled.
items.cn: 分词 dominatus 描述被统治、被控制的状态。

items.en: English formed the verb dominate from the Latin stem; exact first use is uncertain.
items.cn: 英语从拉丁词干造出动词 dominate，确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: The sense widened from people to markets, conversations and towers on a skyline.
items.cn: 词义从人扩展到市场、谈话，以及天际线上的塔。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the domin stem; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of control and prominence.
note.cn: 形近组守着 domin 词干；近义组收的是表示控制与突出地位的动词。

entries.definition: The adjective describing whoever or whatever dominates.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「占主导地位的」，描述正在支配的那一方。

entries.definition: The noun for the act or state of dominating.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「支配、统治」，指支配的行为或状态。

entries.definition: A person or thing that dominates.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「支配者」，指施行支配的人或物。

entries.definition: To direct or restrain something; it stresses management rather than superiority.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「控制、管理」，强调管理而非地位高低。

entries.definition: To prove stronger in the end, often after a struggle.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「占上风、最终取胜」，常含经过较量之意。

entries.definition: To be more important or noticeable than something else, or to cast shade over it.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「使相形见绌、遮蔽」，兼有更重要与投下阴影两义。

normalIntro.en: These hooks follow the real dominus family and the three arenas where dominating happens.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子沿着真实的 dominus 词族，以及支配发生的三种场合。

normal.en: Dominus is the master, so dominate is to act as that master.
normal.cn: dominus 是主人，dominate 就是扮演这个主人。

normal.en: Domination and dominator come straight from the same stem.
normal.cn: domination 与 dominator 直接从同一词干变来。

normal.en: Markets, talks and games can all be dominated by one side.
normal.cn: 市场、谈话与比赛都可能被一方主导。

normal.en: A tower dominates a skyline by filling the view from every street.
normal.cn: 塔高耸于天际线，是因为从每条街望过去都占满视野。

normal.en: The passive form be dominated by means the power lies with someone else.
normal.cn: 被动形式 be dominated by 表示权力在别人手里。

abstract.en: Picture a long shadow from one tower reaching every roof in the town.
abstract.cn: 想象一座塔投下长长的影子，伸到镇上的每一片屋顶。

abstract.en: Picture one voice speaking while the others only nod.
abstract.cn: 想象一个声音在说话，其他人只是点头。

abstract.en: Picture a single name on a scoreboard far ahead of the rest.
abstract.cn: 想象计分板上只有一个名字远远领先。

examples.en: One chain dominates the coffee market in this city.
examples.cn: 一家连锁店主导着这座城市的咖啡市场。

examples.en: The argument dominated dinner conversation for an hour.
examples.cn: 这场争论占据晚餐谈话长达一小时。

examples.en: A tall clock tower dominates the harbour.
examples.cn: 一座高高的钟楼高耸于港口之上。

root: 源自拉丁语 dominari（统治），由 dominus（一家之主）派生，再往前是 domus（房子、家户）。本义是像主人一样对人和物行使支配，后来引申为在某事物中占最大份额，以及在高处俯瞰一片地方。

sensesIntro.en: One verb covers ruling people, filling a conversation or market, and rising above a whole town.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一个动词覆盖了统治他人、占满谈话或市场，以及高高矗立在一座城镇之上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a tower whose shadow reaches every street in the town.
core.cn: 核心意象：一座塔，影子伸到镇上的每一条街。

branches.en: PEOPLE AND MARKETS: the first sense is direct power over others.
branches.cn: 人物与市场线：第一个义项是对他人的直接支配。

branches.en: THE SHARE: the second sense is dominance measured in attention or quantity.
branches.cn: 份额线：第二个义项是以注意力或数量衡量的主导。

branches.en: HEIGHT: the third sense is physical dominance over a view.
branches.cn: 高度线：第三个义项是在视野中的物理性高踞。

branches.en: Power over people and power over a conversation are two scales of the same mastery.
branches.cn: 对人的支配与对谈话的支配，是同一股当家之势的两种尺度。

branches.en: Whatever fills the view or the talk is simply the most dominant thing present.
branches.cn: 占满视野或占满谈话的东西，都只是当下最占主导的那一个。

intro.cn: dominate 把拉丁语动词后缀 -ate 接到同一个 dominus 词干上。

latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 dominus 与 dominari 均有记录，名词 dominatio 也存在。

definition_zh: 概念；观念；想法；看法；念头；（复数）小商品
definition_en: an idea, concept, or belief held in the mind, often vague, personal, or whimsical
core_image: 雾里渐渐成形的一团轮廓：你知道它是什么，却还说不清
scene: 一名女子在餐巾纸上画出大概的轮廓，说明她心里设想的那个主意。 A woman sketches a rough shape on a napkin to show the notion she has in mind.
sceneCN: 这里 notion 是「心里的概念、想法」（第 1 个义项：一般概念）；句意：一位女士在餐巾纸上粗略画出一个形状，说明她心里的想法。图中可辨识物件：餐巾纸、铅笔、粗略的草图、咖啡杯、桌边的笔记本；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: （复数 notions）小商品；杂货（美式英语）

collocations.zh: 完全不知道；对……毫无概念

derivatives.zh: 小商品；杂货（美式复数名词）

senses.title: A Concept: something known in the mind
senses.titleCN: 概念：心里认识到的东西
senses.definition: a general concept or conception formed in the mind
senses.definitionCN: 在头脑中形成的一般概念或观念
senses.example: The notion of fairness varies from culture to culture.
senses.exampleCN: “公平”这一概念因文化而异。
senses.why: Latin notio is an action noun from noscere 'to come to know'. It names the result of knowing, an idea held in the mind, not a written note.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 notio 是 noscere“认识、得知”的动作名词。它命名的是“认知动作的结果”，即心里持有的观念，而不是写下的“笔记”。

senses.title: A Picture in the Mind: a mental image
senses.definition: a mental image or impression of something, often only roughly defined
senses.definitionCN: 对某物的心理图像或印象，常常只有粗略的轮廓
senses.example: I had only a vague notion of the city before I arrived.
senses.exampleCN: 到达之前，我对这座城市只有一个模糊的印象。
senses.why: Knowing something can begin with a shape rather than a definition. The result of that knowing is a picture with soft edges, which English calls a notion.
senses.whyCN: 认识一件事可以从一个轮廓开始，而不是从定义开始。这种认识的结果是一幅边缘模糊的画面，英语就叫 notion。

senses.title: Awareness: having no notion of something
senses.definition: knowledge or awareness of something, chiefly in the phrase have no notion of
senses.definitionCN: 对某事的了解或意识，主要用于 have no notion of 这一说法
senses.example: He had no notion of how much the repairs would cost.
senses.exampleCN: 他完全不知道修理要花多少钱。
senses.why: If notio is the result of knowing, then having no notion is having no result at all: the mind holds nothing on the matter.
senses.whyCN: 如果 notio 是认知的结果，那么 have no notion 就是完全没有结果：心里对这件事空无一物。

senses.title: An Opinion: a view held as true
senses.definition: an opinion or view, especially one held without full proof
senses.definitionCN: 观点或看法，尤指没有充分证据却仍持有的
senses.example: She rejected the old notion that children should be seen and not heard.
senses.exampleCN: 她否定了“孩子只该被看见、不该被听见”的旧观念。
senses.why: By c.1600 the concept in the mind was treated as a view about the world. The mental result now faces outward as an opinion someone holds.
senses.whyCN: 到 17 世纪早期，心里的概念被当作对世界的看法。这个心理结果转向外部，成了某人持有的观点。

senses.title: A Whim: an inclination with no deep reason
senses.titleCN: 念头：没有多少理由的兴之所至
senses.definition: a whimsical or not very rational inclination to do something
senses.definitionCN: 一时兴起、没有多少理性依据的做事倾向
senses.example: On a whim, he took the notion to paint the door blue.
senses.exampleCN: 他一时兴起，动了把门漆成蓝色的念头。
senses.why: A notion can be an idea that arrives without evidence or plan. From 1746 the word also names such a light, self-generated inclination, close to a whim.
senses.whyCN: notion 可以是一个没有证据、没有计划就冒出来的想法。自 1746 年起，这个词也指这种轻飘飘、自发产生的倾向，接近 whim。

senses.title: An Intention: have a notion to do
senses.definition: an intention or plan, chiefly in the phrase have a notion to do something
senses.definitionCN: 意图或打算，主要用于 「have a notion to do something」 这一说法
senses.example: She had a notion to visit the museum before it closed.
senses.exampleCN: 她打算在博物馆闭馆前去一趟。
senses.why: An inclination that survives long enough becomes an intention. The same mental result now points toward a future action rather than a mere picture.
senses.whyCN: 一种倾向如果持续得够久，就变成打算。同一个心理结果此刻指向未来的行动，而不只是一幅画面。

senses.title: A Vague Belief: I had a notion that
senses.definition: a belief or suspicion held without certainty, often introduced by I had a notion that
senses.definitionCN: 没有把握的信念或猜疑，常由 I had a notion that 引出
senses.example: I had a notion that the keys were still in the car.
senses.exampleCN: 我总觉得钥匙还在车里。
senses.why: The mind's result may be uncertain but still acted on. A notion here is a belief with no firm evidence, the softest form of thinking something is true.
senses.whyCN: 心里的结果可以并不确定，却仍会影响行动。这里的 notion 是没有坚实证据的信念，是“认为某事为真”最柔软的形式。

senses.title: Notions: small goods on a counter
senses.definition: in American English, small useful articles such as thread, pins, and buttons sold in a shop
senses.definitionCN: 美式英语中指针线、别针、纽扣等在商店出售的小件用品
senses.example: The general store kept buttons and thread among its notions.
senses.exampleCN: 这家杂货店把纽扣和线归在小商品里。
senses.why: In 1803 American English used notions for small clever inventions, then for the small goods a dry-goods store sold. The 'bright idea' became a physical trinket.
senses.whyCN: 1803 年美式英语用 notions 指“聪明的小发明”，随后指干货店出售的小商品。“灵光一现的想法”变成了手里的实物小件。

senses.title: The Philosopher's Notion: Cicero's loan translation
senses.titleCN: 哲学家的概念：西塞罗的仿译
senses.definition: in philosophy, a general idea formed by abstraction, especially as Cicero translated Greek ennoia or prolepsis
senses.definitionCN: 哲学中通过抽象形成的一般观念，尤指西塞罗对希腊语 ennoia 或 prolepsis 的仿译
senses.example: The Stoics debated whether a notion could arise before any experience.
senses.exampleCN: 斯多葛派争论概念能否在任何经验之前产生。
senses.why: Cicero needed a Latin word for Greek ennoia 'act of thinking, notion' and prolepsis 'previous notion'. He used notio, the result of noscere, to name an abstract idea in the mind.
senses.whyCN: 西塞罗需要给希腊语 ennoia“思维活动、概念”和 prolepsis“预先形成的概念”找拉丁词。他用了 notio，即 noscere 的结果，来命名心中的抽象观念。

intro.en: Notion comes from Latin notio, an action noun from noscere 'to come to know'. It names the result of knowing, an idea in the mind, and Cicero used it to translate Greek philosophical terms.
intro.cn: notion 来自拉丁语 notio，是 noscere“认识、得知”的动作名词。它命名认知动作的结果，即心中的观念；西塞罗曾用它翻译希腊哲学术语。

items.en: Recorded as nocioun, meaning 'a general concept, conception'.
items.cn: 以 nocioun 的形式记录，意为“一般概念、观念”。

items.en: From Latin notionem (nominative notio) 'concept, conception, idea, notice', an action noun from the past-participle stem of noscere 'come to know'.
items.cn: 来自拉丁语 notionem（主格 notio）“概念、观念、想法、知悉”，是 noscere“认识、得知”过去分词词干的动作名词。

items.en: Noscere traces to PIE *gno- 'to know', the same family that gives know and knowledge.
items.cn: noscere 可追到原始印欧语 *gno-“知道”，与英语 know、knowledge 同族。

items.en: Cicero formed notio as a loan translation of Greek ennoia 'act of thinking, notion' or prolepsis 'previous notion'.
items.cn: 西塞罗用 notio 仿译希腊语 ennoia“思维活动、概念”或 prolepsis“预先形成的概念”。

items.en: The sense 'opinion, view' is recorded; the modern word now covers both a concept and a stance.
items.cn: 记录到“意见、看法”义；现代这个词同时覆盖“概念”和“立场”。

items.en: The sense 'whim, not very rational inclination' appears in 1746, and American English notions 'small goods' in 1803, by way of 'clever little inventions'.
items.cn: 1746 年出现“念头、不太理性的倾向”义；1803 年美式英语出现 notions“小商品”义，经由“聪明的小发明”这一想法。

note.en: The first group is chosen for spelling and sound; the second for overlapping meaning, so form and sense stay separate.
note.cn: 第一组按拼写和读音挑选，第二组按词义重叠挑选，使词形与词义分开。

entries.definition: attention or a written announcement. It comes from Latin notitia 'knowledge', a close relative of notio, not from notion itself.
entries.definitionCN: 注意；书面通知。它来自拉丁语 notitia“知悉”，是 notio 的近亲，而不是 notion 的派生词。

entries.definition: a country and its people. It looks close to notion but comes from Latin natio 'birth, race', with no shared root.
entries.definitionCN: 国家与国民。它拼写像 notion，但来自拉丁语 natio“出生、族类”，没有共同词根。

entries.definition: a system of written symbols. It comes from Latin nota 'mark', a different branch from notio.
entries.definitionCN: 符号体系。它来自拉丁语 nota“记号”，与 notio 是不同分支。

entries.definition: the broadest word for something in the mind. Notion is narrower and often suggests something vague or personal.
entries.definitionCN: 表示“心中所想”最宽泛的词。notion 更窄，常暗示模糊或个人的成分。

entries.definition: a general idea formed by abstraction. It is more formal and precise than notion.
entries.definitionCN: 通过抽象形成的一般观念。它比 notion 更正式、更精确。

entries.definition: acceptance that something is true. It is stronger than a notion, which may be little more than a hunch.
entries.definitionCN: 接受某事为真。它比 notion 更强，notion 可能只是一种直觉。

normalIntro.en: Real links only: notio is the result of noscere 'to know', and English notice, notify and notorious belong to the same knowing family.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实联系：notio 是 noscere“知道”的结果，英语 notice、notify、notorious 都属于同一个“认知”词族。

normal.en: Notio is an action noun from noscere 'to come to know': it is the result of knowing, not a written note.
normal.cn: notio 是 noscere“认识”的动作名词：它是认知的结果，不是写下的笔记。

normal.en: Notice, notify and notorious all go back to the same 'know' root, so the not- in notion is a knowing not-.
normal.cn: notice、notify、notorious 都回到同一个“知道”词根，所以 notion 里的 not- 是“认知”的 not-。

normal.en: Have no notion of means the mind holds nothing at all on the subject.
normal.cn: have no notion of 意思是心里对这件事空无一物。

normal.en: A vague notion is an idea whose edges have not been drawn yet.
normal.cn: a vague notion 是边缘还没画清楚的观念。

normal.en: Notions on a shop counter are small goods, a sense that grew out of 'clever little inventions'.
normal.cn: 柜台上的 notions 是小商品，这个义项从“聪明的小发明”长出来。

abstract.en: Picture a shape forming in mist: you can point at it, but you cannot trace its outline.
abstract.cn: 想象雾中渐渐成形的轮廓：你能指向它，却描不出边界。

abstract.en: The same shape can harden into an opinion or soften into a whim.
abstract.cn: 同一团轮廓可以硬化成观点，也可以软化成一时兴起。

abstract.en: Follow it into a shop and it shrinks to a button on a notions counter.
abstract.cn: 跟着它走进商店，它就缩成小商品柜台上一枚纽扣。

examples.en: He had no notion of how difficult the language would be.
examples.cn: 他完全不知道这门语言会有多难。

examples.en: The notion that money brings happiness is widely questioned.
examples.cn: “金钱带来幸福”这一观念受到广泛质疑。

examples.en: The old shop sold needles, ribbons, and other notions.
examples.cn: 那家老店出售针、缎带和其他小商品。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「诺神」——脑子里“诺”的一声，仿佛神仙递来一个模糊念头 → notion 概念、想法

root: 拉丁语 notio“概念、想法”，是 noscere“认识、得知”的动作名词，追到原始印欧语 *gno-“知道”；notio 是认知动作的结果，不是“笔记”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of notion all name something the mind knows. The knowing can be a concept, a picture, an opinion, a whim, an intention, a hunch, a shop-counter trinket, or a philosopher's abstraction.
sensesIntro.cn: notion 的九个义项都在命名“心里知道的东西”。这种知道可以是概念、画面、看法、一时兴起、打算、直觉、柜台小商品，或哲学家的抽象观念。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a shape forming in the mind, known before it is clearly defined.
core.cn: 核心意象：心中渐渐成形的轮廓，先被知道，后才有清楚定义。

branches.en: THE KNOWN SHAPE: a general concept, and a mental picture with soft edges.
branches.cn: 被认知的轮廓：一般概念，以及边缘模糊的心理画面。

branches.en: AWARENESS: having a notion, or having no notion at all.
branches.cn: 知晓：有概念，或完全没有概念。

branches.en: VIEW AND BELIEF: an opinion held as true, and a hunch held without certainty.
branches.cn: 看法与信念：自认为真的观点，以及没有把握的直觉。

branches.en: INCLINATION AND INTENTION: a whim that arrives, and a plan that stays.
branches.cn: 倾向与意图：突然到来的念头，以及留下来成为打算的念头。

branches.en: FROM TRINKET TO ABSTRACTION: small shop goods, and Cicero's philosophical concept.
branches.cn: 从小商品到抽象：柜台小货，以及西塞罗的哲学概念。

intro.en: Notion is the Latin noun notio in English form. Its family adds -al, -ly and -ity, while notice, notify and notorious belong to the same noscere 'know' root.
intro.cn: notion 是拉丁语名词 notio 的英语形式。它的词族加 -al、-ly、-ity，而 notice、notify、notorious 属于同一个 noscere“知道”词根。

latinIntro.en: Latin notio 'concept, idea' is an action noun from noscere 'come to know', whose participle notus 'known' also underlies notice and notify. The deepest root is PIE *gno- 'to know'.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 notio“概念、想法”是 noscere“认识”的动作名词；其分词 notus“已知的”也支撑着 notice 与 notify。最深层词根是原始印欧语 *gno-“知道”。

items.meaning: a concept or idea in the mind
items.meaningCN: 心中的概念或想法（-ion 构成动作或结果名词）
items.example: The notion of progress is not universal.
items.exampleCN: “进步”这一观念并非普世皆同。

items.meaningCN: 概念上的；理论上的（-al 构成形容词）
items.example: The cost is notional until the contract is signed.
items.exampleCN: 合同签订前，这项费用只是名义上的。

items.meaningCN: 概念上；名义上（-ly 构成副词）
items.example: The two departments are notionally separate.
items.exampleCN: 这两个部门名义上是分开的。

items.meaningCN: 概念性（-ity 构成名词，哲学用语）
items.example: The paper questions the notionality of pure sense data.
items.exampleCN: 这篇论文质疑纯粹感觉材料的概念性。

items.meaning: small useful goods sold in a shop
items.meaningCN: 小商品；杂货（复数形式，美式英语）
items.example: She bought thread and buttons at the notions counter.
items.exampleCN: 她在小商品柜台买了线和纽扣。

items.meaningCN: 注意；通知（同出 notus“已知的”）
items.example: A notice was posted on the door.

items.meaning: to make someone know; to inform
items.meaningCN: 通知；告知（-ify 构成动词）
items.example: Please notify the office of any change.
items.exampleCN: 如有变动，请通知办公室。

items.meaningCN: 通知；告示（-ication 构成名词）
items.example: The app sends a notification when the file is ready.
items.exampleCN: 文件准备好时，应用会发出通知。

items.meaning: well known, usually for something bad
items.meaningCN: 臭名昭著的；众所周知的（-orious 构成形容词）
items.example: The road is notorious for winter accidents.
items.exampleCN: 这条路因冬季事故频发而臭名昭著。

latinEntries.meaning: to come to know, learn, recognize

definition_zh: 解决；协议；定居点；结算；沉降
definition_en: the ending of an argument, an official agreement, a place where people have settled, the payment of a debt, or the sinking of land
core_image: 几张签好字的纸叠在一起，桌上的争执终于停下
scene: 两国达成了解决方案。 The two countries reached a settlement.
sceneCN: 这里 settlement 是「解决」（第 1 个义项）；句意：两国达成了解决方案。

senses.title: Resolution
senses.definition: the ending of an argument or disagreement
senses.definitionCN: 争论或分歧的结束
senses.example: The two countries reached a settlement.
senses.exampleCN: 两国达成了解决方案。
senses.why: This is the core abstract sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是核心的抽象义项。

senses.title: Official agreement
senses.definition: a formal agreement that ends a dispute
senses.definitionCN: 结束争端的正式协议
senses.example: They signed a settlement after talks.
senses.exampleCN: 谈判后他们签署了协议。
senses.why: A resolution is often written down.
senses.whyCN: 解决方案常常被写下来。

senses.title: Place of living
senses.definition: a place where people have made their home
senses.definitionCN: 人们安家落户的地方
senses.example: A small settlement grew by the river.
senses.exampleCN: 河边渐渐形成一个小定居点。
senses.why: People settle, and the place is a settlement.
senses.whyCN: 人们定居下来，这地方就成了定居点。

senses.title: Payment
senses.definition: the payment of a debt or claim
senses.definitionCN: 对债务或索赔的支付
senses.example: The settlement arrived after the sale.
senses.exampleCN: 交易完成后结算款到账了。
senses.why: A debt comes to rest when paid.
senses.whyCN: 债务在付清时落定。

senses.title: Sinking of ground
senses.definition: the slow sinking of land or a building
senses.definitionCN: 土地或建筑物的缓慢下沉
senses.example: The settlement of the ground cracked the wall.
senses.exampleCN: 地面沉降使墙壁开裂。
senses.why: The ground also settles.
senses.whyCN: 地面也会落定下沉。

intro.en: Settlement is settle plus -ment, so it names the result of coming to rest.
intro.cn: settlement 由 settle 加 -ment 构成，指「落定」带来的结果。

items.en: Setl meant a seat.
items.cn: setl 意为座位。

items.en: Settle meant to come to rest.
items.cn: settle 意为落定。

items.en: Settlement named a colony.
items.cn: settlement 指定居点。

items.en: Settlement named a legal agreement.
items.cn: settlement 指法律协议。

items.en: Settlement named the paying of a debt.
items.cn: settlement 指债务的结清。

note.en: Settlement is compared with similar-looking words and with words for agreements and colonies.
note.cn: 把 settlement 与形近词以及表示协议和定居点的词作比较。

entries.definition: a person who settles
entries.definitionCN: 定居者

entries.definition: something said or written
entries.definitionCN: 陈述

entries.definition: a feeling or opinion
entries.definitionCN: 情感；意见

entries.definition: an arrangement accepted by all
entries.definitionCN: 协议

entries.definition: the solving of a problem
entries.definitionCN: 解决

entries.definition: a place settled by a group
entries.definitionCN: 殖民地；聚居地

normalIntro.en: Settlement is what remains after settling: a signed paper, a village, a paid bill, or sunken ground.
normalIntro.cn: settlement 是「落定」之后留下的东西：签好的纸、成形的村庄、付清的账单或下沉的地面。

normal.en: The dispute ended in a settlement.
normal.cn: 争端以和解告终。

normal.en: The peace settlement was signed in May.
normal.cn: 和平协议在五月签署。

normal.en: A settlement grew around the well.
normal.cn: 一个定居点在井边发展起来。

normal.en: The settlement cleared the debt.
normal.cn: 这笔结算清偿了债务。

normal.en: Ground settlement damaged the road.
normal.cn: 地面沉降损坏了道路。

abstract.en: A settlement is a place where motion becomes a home.
abstract.cn: 定居点，是运动变成家的地方。

abstract.en: Agreement is a bridge built from both sides.
abstract.cn: 协议是从两岸同时修起的一座桥。

abstract.en: Even the ground remembers the weight above it.
abstract.cn: 连地面也记得压在它上面的重量。

examples.en: The two countries reached a settlement.
examples.cn: 两国达成了解决方案。

examples.en: A small settlement grew by the river.
examples.cn: 河边渐渐形成一个小定居点。

examples.en: The settlement of the ground cracked the wall.
examples.cn: 地面沉降使墙壁开裂。

dict_mnemonic.text: settlement 由 settle（安定、解决）加名词后缀 -ment 构成，指解决、协议、定居点或结算。

root: 由 settle（源自古英语 setl，座位）加 -ment 构成，核心义「落定之后的结果」。

sensesIntro.en: Settlement means a resolution, an agreement, a colony, a payment, or the sinking of ground.
sensesIntro.cn: settlement 意为解决、协议、定居点、结算或沉降。

core.en: The state or place that results from settling.
core.cn: 落定之后形成的状态或地方。

branches.en: A dispute brought to rest.
branches.cn: 被平息的争端。

branches.en: The written form of that rest.
branches.cn: 这种平息的书面形式。

branches.en: A place where people rest.
branches.cn: 人们安家的地方。

branches.en: A debt brought to rest.
branches.cn: 被了结的债务。

branches.en: Ground coming to rest.
branches.cn: 地面的落定。

intro.en: Settlement is settle plus the noun suffix -ment.
intro.cn: settlement 是 settle 加名词后缀 -ment。

latinIntro.en: The base settle is Germanic; Latin sedere, to sit, is only a semantic parallel.
latinIntro.cn: 词基 settle 属日耳曼语；拉丁语 sedere（坐）只是语义对应词。

items.example: The settlement was fair to both sides.
items.exampleCN: 这份协议对双方都公平。
海岸边分布着几个定居点。

items.meaning: the act of coming to rest

items.exampleCN: 重新安置计划获得了批准。
未结算的索赔仍未了结。

definition_zh: 北方的；北部的；朝北的；来自北方的
definition_en: of, in or facing the north; coming from the north; belonging to the northern part of a country or the world
core_image: 一片朝北的坡地上，矮树被风吹得贴向地面，枝头挂着一层白霜
scene: 山坡上的矮树全都朝一侧歪着长，枝头挂着一层白霜，风一整天没停。 The northern half of the country is colder, with snow from November.
sceneCN: 这里是「北方的、北部的」（第 1 个义项：位于北方或朝北的），句意为这个国家的北半部更冷，从十一月就开始下雪。图中可辨识物件：矮树、白霜、坡地。

pos.zh: 北方的；北部的；来自北方的

derivatives.zh: northern 的基础词，古英语 norþ 传下，义为「北；北方」
由 northern 加 -er（属于某地的人）构成，义为「北方人」
由 north 加 -erly 构成，义为「偏北的；来自北方的」

senses.title: Of a place that lies in or faces the north
senses.titleCN: 北方的；位于北部的；朝北的
senses.definition: located in the north, or pointing toward the north
senses.definitionCN: 位于北方，或者朝向北方
senses.example: The northern half of the country is colder, with snow from November.
senses.exampleCN: 这个国家的北半部更冷，从十一月就开始下雪。
senses.why: The Old English adjective added an ending meaning belonging to a direction, so northern simply says that a place belongs to the north rather than naming the direction itself.
senses.whyCN: 古英语的形容词形式加了一个表示「属于某个方向」的词尾，所以 northern 只是说某地属于北方，而不是给方向本身命名。

senses.title: Coming from the north
senses.definition: blowing or moving from the north, said especially of winds and weather
senses.definitionCN: 从北方吹来或移来，尤指风与天气
senses.example: A northern wind brought frost to the valley overnight.
senses.exampleCN: 一股北风一夜之间把霜带进了山谷。
senses.why: A wind is named by where it starts, so the same adjective that marks location on a map also marks the origin of cold air, which is why weather reports lean on it.
senses.whyCN: 风是按它来的方向命名的，所以同一个标出地图位置的形容词也用来标出冷空气的来处，天气预报才如此依赖它。

senses.title: Belonging to the northern part of a country or the world
senses.titleCN: 北部地区的；北方地区的
senses.definition: relating to the northern region of a country or of the world, often written with a capital in regional names
senses.definitionCN: 与国家或世界的北部地区有关，用于地区名称时常首字母大写
senses.example: Northern Ireland has its own assembly and its own legal traditions.
senses.exampleCN: 北爱尔兰有自己的议会和自己的法律传统。
senses.why: When a region becomes a political or cultural unit, the adjective turns into part of its proper name, so northern stops describing and starts labeling.
senses.whyCN: 当一个地区成为政治或文化单位，这个形容词就进入它的专名，于是 northern 从描述转为标签。

intro.en: Northern is the Old English adjective built on north with a suffix meaning belonging to a direction; the comparative force of its Germanic ancestor has faded.
intro.cn: northern 是古英语里在 north 上加「属于某方向」词尾构成的形容词；它日耳曼语祖先带有的比较意味已经消失。

items.en: The ancestor of this adjective carried a comparative ending, so it meant roughly the more northward one; the exact reconstructed form is inferred.
items.cn: 这个形容词的祖先把比较级词尾带在身上，大致表示「更靠北的那一个」；确切的重构形式属于推断。

items.en: Norþerne joined norþ to the suffix -erne, meaning belonging to the north, and it described northern winds, lands and peoples.
items.cn: norþerne 把 norþ 接到词尾 -erne 上，表示「属于北方」，用来形容北风、北方土地与北方部族。

items.en: Middle English leveled the ending to -ern and fixed the spelling northern, while the old comparative sense dropped away.
items.cn: 中古英语把词尾拉平为 -ern，拼写固定为 northern，旧的比较意味也随之脱落。

items.en: Writers applied northern to climates, winds, coastlines and the northern lights, widening it from a local word to a geographic one.
items.cn: 十六至十八世纪的作者把 northern 用于气候、风、海岸线与北极光，使它从本地用词扩展为地理用词。

items.en: Modern English uses northern for hemispheres and regions and in proper names such as Northern Ireland, where the capital N marks a political unit.
items.cn: 现代英语用 northern 指半球与地区，也用于 Northern Ireland 这类专名，那里的首字母大写标出一个政治单位。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the same north base through its noun, wind adjective and person noun; the near-meaning group sets northern against the other direction adjectives.
note.cn: 形近组沿同一个 north 底座，收它的名词、风向形容词与人称名词；近义组把 northern 与其他方向形容词放在一起对照。

entries.definition: The direction itself, the base from which northern is built.
entries.definitionCN: 方向本身，也是构成 northern 的底座。

entries.definition: A wind blowing from the north or a direction close to north.
entries.definitionCN: 从北方吹来的风，或接近北方的方向。

entries.definition: A person who lives in or comes from the north.
entries.definitionCN: 住在北方或来自北方的人。

entries.definition: Of or in the south, the mirror image of northern.
entries.definitionCN: 位于南方或朝南的，是 northern 的镜像。

entries.definition: Of the north and its cold forests, a formal word used in science and poetry.
entries.definitionCN: 指北方及其寒冷森林，是科学与诗歌里的正式用词。

entries.definition: Of the far north around the pole, colder and more extreme than northern.
entries.definitionCN: 指极地附近的极北，比 northern 更冷也更极端。

normalIntro.en: The word is north wearing a suffix that means belonging to, and its three uses are the place, the wind and the region.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是 north 披上表示「属于」的词尾，它的三种用法分别是地点、风与地区。

normal.en: Northern is north plus -ern, the same ending that turns west into western and south into southern.
normal.cn: northern 是 north 加 -ern，正是把 west 变成 western、把 south 变成 southern 的那个词尾。

normal.en: The Old English form was norþerne, with a longer ending that already meant belonging to the north.
normal.cn: 古英语形式是 norþerne，词尾更长，那时就已经表示「属于北方」。

normal.en: Its Germanic ancestor was comparative, so northern once sounded like the more northward one, though that shade is gone today.
normal.cn: 它的日耳曼语祖先是比较级，所以 northern 曾经听起来像「更靠北的那一个」，不过这层意味今天已经没有了。

normal.en: A northern wind is named by its starting point, which is why the same adjective serves both maps and weather.
normal.cn: 北方的风是按起点命名的，所以同一个形容词既能用在地图上，也能用在天气里。

normal.en: A capital N in Northern Ireland marks a proper name, not a description of the weather.
normal.cn: Northern Ireland 里的首字母大写标出一个专名，而不是描述天气。

abstract.en: An adjective built to say belonging makes geography into identity: a place, a wind and a people can all be northern.
abstract.cn: 一个表示「属于」的形容词把地理变成身份：一个地方、一股风、一群人，都可以是 northern。

abstract.en: The comparative ending died, but its direction survived, so northern still quietly points to one end of the map.
abstract.cn: 比较级词尾死了，方向却活了下来，所以 northern 仍在悄悄指向地图的一端。

abstract.en: Northern is what a name becomes when a direction is organized into a region with borders and institutions.
abstract.cn: 当一个方向被组织成有边界和机构的地区，northern 就是它变成名称的样子。

examples.en: The northern half of the country is colder, with snow from November.
examples.cn: 这个国家的北半部更冷，从十一月就开始下雪。

examples.en: A northern wind brought frost to the valley overnight.
examples.cn: 一股北风一夜之间把霜带进了山谷。

examples.en: Northern Ireland has its own assembly and its own legal traditions.
examples.cn: 北爱尔兰有自己的议会和自己的法律传统。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「诺森」——北边的坡上矮树都被风吹歪了；northern 就是北方的。

root: 古英语 norþerne，由 norþ（北）加 -erne（属于某方向）构成；其日耳曼语祖先带比较级词尾，现代英语中该意味已消失。

sensesIntro.en: The core is belonging to the north; the senses then split into location and facing, the origin of winds, and the political region.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「属于北方」；义项由此分出位置与朝向、风的来处，以及政治意义上的地区。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: low trees on a north-facing slope, bent by wind and edged with frost.
core.cn: 核心意象：朝北坡地上的矮树被风压弯，枝头镶着一层白霜。

branches.en: a farmhouse on a slope that faces the cold end of the sky
branches.cn: 坡地上朝向天空冷端的农舍

branches.en: a map with the upper half shaded for the colder months
branches.cn: 上半部分为寒冷月份涂色的地图

branches.en: frost forming overnight after a northern wind
branches.cn: 北风过后一夜结出的霜

branches.en: a regional flag flying over a northern assembly
branches.cn: 北方议会楼上升起的地区旗帜

branches.en: the same word marking weather and a political border
branches.cn: 同一个词既标天气，也标政治边界

intro.en: The word is a direction noun plus a suffix of belonging, and English later added the endings for its person noun and its wind adjective.
intro.cn: 这个词是方位名词加「属于」词尾，英语后来又添上构成人称名词与风向形容词的词尾。

latinIntro.en: Northern has no reliable Latin cognate; Latin names the north with septentrionalis, a word built from the seven stars of the Great Bear, which is unrelated in origin.
latinIntro.cn: northern 没有可靠的拉丁同族词；拉丁语用「septentrionalis」表示「北方的」，那是从大熊座七星得名的词，来源与此无关。

definition_zh: 松的；不紧的；宽松的；不受约束的；不严谨的；释放
definition_en: not firmly fixed or tied, not fitting closely, free from control or restraint, not strict or precise, or to set something free
core_image: 一根原本绷紧的绳子忽然松下来，绳结松垮地垂在木桩边
scene: 清晨的码头上，一条小船的缆绳在桩上松了半圈，船身轻轻晃动。 The rope came loose during the night and the boat drifted a little.
sceneCN: 这里 loose 是「松的、不紧的」（第 1 个义项：没有牢牢固定）；句意为夜里缆绳松了，船稍微漂开。图中可辨识物件：码头、缆绳、木桩、小船。

pos.zh: 松的；不紧的；宽松的；不受约束的；不严谨的

collocations.zh: 未了结的细节；松散的线头

derivatives.zh: 由 loose 加 -ly 构成，义为「松散地；不严格地」
由 loose 加 -en 构成，义为「使变松；松开」
由 loose 加 -ness 构成，义为「松弛；松散」

senses.title: Not firmly fixed or tied
senses.definition: not held tightly in place, so that it can move, slip or come off
senses.definitionCN: 没有被牢牢固定在原位，因此会移动、滑动或脱落
senses.example: One of the screws is loose and the shelf wobbles.
senses.exampleCN: 有一颗螺丝松了，架子摇摇晃晃。
senses.why: The core image is tension gone slack: what should grip no longer grips, so the first sense names anything that can move because it is not held fast.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是张力消失、变松：本该咬住的不再咬住，所以第一个义项指任何因为没被牢牢固定而能移动的东西。

senses.title: Not fitting closely
senses.definition: of clothes or coverings, larger than the body so that it does not press against it
senses.definitionCN: 指衣服或覆盖物比身体大，不会紧贴身体
senses.example: He wore a loose shirt to the interview.
senses.exampleCN: 他穿着一件宽松的衬衫去面试。
senses.why: When cloth stops pressing on the body, the same slackness that lets a screw slip lets air move under a garment; the sense moves from fastening to fit.
senses.whyCN: 当布料不再压住身体，让螺丝滑动的那种松弛便让空气能在衣服下面流动；义项从「固定」转到「合身程度」。

senses.title: Free from control or restraint
senses.definition: not kept in a cage, prison or strict system, and able to move or act freely
senses.definitionCN: 没有被关在笼子、监狱或严格体系里，能够自由移动或行动
senses.example: The gate was left open and the dog got loose.
senses.exampleCN: 大门没关，狗跑了出去。
senses.why: A thing not tied down is also not controlled; once the physical rope is gone, the word can describe anyone or anything escaping restraint.
senses.whyCN: 没有被捆住的东西也不受控制；一旦具体的绳子消失，这个词就能形容任何摆脱约束的人或物。

senses.title: Not strict or precise
senses.definition: of language, rules or thinking, not exact and allowing more than one interpretation
senses.definitionCN: 指语言、规则或思考不精确，允许不止一种解释
senses.example: The article gives only a loose definition of the term.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇文章只给这个术语下了一个宽泛的定义。
senses.why: A tight knot leaves no room to move; a statement that leaves room to move is felt to be tied just as loosely, so precision becomes the thing that is not fastened down.
senses.whyCN: 系紧的结不留活动的余地；一句留有余地的话也被觉得系得同样松，于是精确性成了那个没被固定住的东西。

senses.title: To set free or let go
senses.definition: to release an animal, a person or a held object, or to fire an arrow or shot
senses.definitionCN: 放开动物、人或握住的物体，也可指射出箭或子弹
senses.example: The keeper loosed the dogs at sunset.
senses.exampleCN: 日落后，看守人把狗放开了。
senses.why: The adjective describes the state of being untied; the verb is the act that produces that state, so the same word becomes the hand opening.
senses.whyCN: 形容词描述的是「已被解开」的状态；动词则是产生这种状态的动作，于是同一个词变成了张开的手。

intro.en: Loose is generally traced to a Germanic adjective for slackness and freedom; English later built loosely, loosen and looseness on it.
intro.cn: loose 一般认为源自一个表示松弛与自由的日耳曼语形容词；英语后来在它之上构成了 loosely、loosen 与 looseness。

items.en: The adjective is generally traced to Old Norse lauss, meaning loose, free or dissolute, which entered English during the Norse settlements.
items.cn: 这个形容词一般认为源自古诺斯语 lauss，意为松的、自由的、放纵的，在诺斯人定居时期进入英语。

items.en: The reconstructed Germanic form means loose or free; German los and Dutch los are close relatives, and the English suffix -less grows from the same family.
items.cn: 重构的日耳曼语形式意为松的、自由的；德语 los 与荷兰语 los 是近亲，英语后缀 -less 也出自同一词族。

items.en: Middle English loose appears as an adjective for what is not bound, and a verb meaning to set free grows beside it.
items.cn: 中古英语的 loose 已是形容词，指没有被捆住的东西；旁边又长出表示「释放」的动词。

items.en: The word spreads from ropes and cages to clothes, morals and language, giving phrases such as loose woman and loose translation.
items.cn: 这个词从绳索与笼子扩展到衣服、品行与语言，产生 loose woman 与 loose translation 之类的说法。

items.en: Modern English keeps the physical and abstract senses side by side and builds the family loosely, loosen and looseness; it is a different word from lose, which means to misplace or be deprived of.
items.cn: 现代英语让具体的与抽象的义项并排存在，并构成 loosely、loosen、looseness 等同族词；它与表示「丢失、失去」的 lose 是不同的词。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers family forms and the easily confused lose; the near-meaning group gathers words for slackness, loose fit and freedom.
note.cn: 形近组收同族形式以及容易混淆的 lose；近义组收表示松弛、宽松与自由的词。

entries.definition: In a slack, relaxed or inexact way.
entries.definitionCN: 由 loose 加 -ly 构成，义为「松散地；不严格地」。

entries.definition: To make or become less tight.
entries.definitionCN: 由 loose 加 -en 构成，义为「使变松；松开」。

entries.definition: The quality or state of being loose.
entries.definitionCN: 由 loose 加 -ness 构成，义为「松弛；松散」。

entries.definition: To no longer have something, or to fail to keep it.
entries.definitionCN: 只是拼写和读音相近，词源不同；义为「丢失；失去」。

entries.definition: Not tight, and lacking the usual tension.
entries.definitionCN: 松弛的；强调绳索或肌肉缺少张力，与 loose 近义。

entries.definition: Of clothes, very wide and hanging loosely.
entries.definitionCN: 衣服宽大下垂的；多指版型，不指固定是否牢固。

entries.definition: Not controlled or limited by another person or system.
entries.definitionCN: 自由的；强调不受人或制度限制，不指物理松紧。

entries.definition: Not strict enough in enforcing rules.
entries.definitionCN: 松懈的；多指规则执行不严，源自不同词根。

normalIntro.en: The word is anchored in a Germanic adjective for slackness and freedom, and its family keeps returning to things that are not held tight.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词锚定在一个表示松弛与自由的日耳曼语形容词上，同族词反复回到没有被紧紧固定住的东西。

normal.en: Loose starts in Old Norse lauss, a word for free as well as slack; the physical and the social senses were there from the beginning.
normal.cn: loose 源自古诺斯语 lauss，这个词既指松弛也指自由；具体的与社会的义项从一开始就都在。

normal.en: The suffix -less comes from the same Germanic family, which is why less and loose both carry the idea of being without.
normal.cn: -less 这个后缀出自同一日耳曼词族，所以 less 与 loose 都带着「没有、缺少」的意思。

normal.en: Loosen adds -en to loose and means to make less tight; loosely adds -ly and describes the manner.
normal.cn: loosen 在 loose 后加 -en，表示「使变松」；loosely 加 -ly，描述做事的方式。

normal.en: Loose change is coins carried loose in a pocket, not fastened into a wallet or roll.
normal.cn: loose change 是散放在口袋里、没有捆进钱包或纸卷的零钱。

normal.en: Do not confuse loose with lose: loose is slack, lose is to no longer have something.
normal.cn: 不要把 loose 与 lose 弄混：loose 是松，lose 是失去某物。

abstract.en: A knot that has gone slack can still look tied, which is why loose rules and loose talk are hard to notice at first.
abstract.cn: 松掉的结看上去仍像系着，所以宽松的规则与随意的言辞起初不容易被察觉。

abstract.en: Freedom and slackness share one word because both mean that nothing is holding you in place.
abstract.cn: 自由与松弛共用一个词，因为两者都意味着没有东西把你固定住。

abstract.en: A loose end is not a failure; it is simply a thread the story has not tied yet.
abstract.cn: 松着的线头不是失败，它只是故事还没系上的一根线。

examples.en: One of the screws is loose and the shelf wobbles.
examples.cn: 有一颗螺丝松了，架子摇摇晃晃。

examples.en: He wore a loose shirt to the interview.
examples.cn: 他穿着一件宽松的衬衫去面试。

examples.en: The gate was left open and the dog got loose.
examples.cn: 大门没关，狗跑了出去。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「露丝」——衣服露在外头，松松垮垮；loose 就是松的、宽松的。

root: 一般认为源自古诺斯语 lauss（松的、自由的），与古英语 leas（缺少、虚假）同属一个日耳曼词族，并衍生出 -less；没有可靠的拉丁同族词。注意与 lose（丢失）区分。

sensesIntro.en: The core is tension released; the senses divide into physical slackness, loose fit, freedom from control, imprecise wording, and the act of setting something free.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是张力被放开；义项由此分出物理上的松弛、衣服的宽松、不受控制、措辞不精确，以及把某物放开的动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a rope that was taut going slack, its knot drooping beside the post.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根原本绷紧的绳子松下来，绳结垂在木桩边。

branches.en: a screw turning without grip
branches.cn: 一颗失去咬合、转得空转的螺丝

branches.en: a shirt hanging away from the body
branches.cn: 衬衫离开身体垂着

branches.en: a dog slipping through an open gate
branches.cn: 狗从敞开的门里溜出去

branches.en: a translation that keeps only the general sense
branches.cn: 只保留大意的一段翻译

branches.en: a hand opening and letting go
branches.cn: 一只手张开、放开

intro.en: The word comes from a Germanic adjective of slackness and freedom; three English suffixes turn it into the adverb, the verb and the noun of the family.
intro.cn: 这个词来自一个表示松弛与自由的日耳曼语形容词；三个英语后缀把它变成同族的副词、动词与名词。

latinIntro.en: Loose comes from Old Norse and Germanic stock; Latin laxus also means slack, but it is not a reliable cognate, so no Latin family is listed.
latinIntro.cn: loose 来自古诺斯语与日耳曼语词族；拉丁语 laxus 虽也表示松弛，但并非可靠同源，因此不列拉丁同族词。

definition_zh: 诗人；写诗的人；有诗心的人
definition_en: a person who writes poems, especially one who treats verse as a craft or a calling; also anyone who sees ordinary life with a poet's imagination
core_image: 一个人伏在桌前，把心里翻涌的东西一行行改成有节奏的句子，废纸团堆在脚边
scene: 深夜的屋子里只亮着一盏台灯，纸页被反复涂改，桌边的茶早已凉透。 The old poet kept rewriting the last line until dawn.
sceneCN: 这里 poet 是「诗人」（第 1 个义项：以写诗为手艺或志业的人）；句意为这位老诗人反复改写最后一行，一直改到天亮。图中可辨识物件：台灯、涂改过的纸页、凉透的茶杯。

pos.zh: 诗人；写诗的人；有诗心的人

derivatives.zh: 由 poet 换接集合名词后缀 -ry 构成，指诗歌这一体裁的整体
由希腊词干 poie- 加形容词后缀 -tic 构成，义为「诗的；富有诗意的」
由 poetic 加 -s 构成，义为「诗学；诗歌理论」
由 poet 加阴性后缀 -ess 构成，旧指「女诗人」，今已少用

senses.title: A person who writes poems
senses.definition: a person who writes poems, especially one who treats verse as a craft or a calling
senses.definitionCN: 写诗的人，尤指把写诗当作一门手艺或志业的人
senses.example: The poet read three new poems at the small bookshop.
senses.exampleCN: 这位诗人在那家小书店里朗诵了三首新作。
senses.why: Greek poietes began as a word for any maker, and only the habit of calling the verse-maker a maker narrowed it to the writer of poems.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 poietes 原本泛指「制作者」，只是人们习惯把制作诗句的人叫作制作者，词义才收窄为写诗的人。

senses.title: An officially appointed verse writer
senses.definition: a poet formally chosen to write verse for a state, a city or an institution on special occasions
senses.definitionCN: 受国家、城市或机构正式委任，在特定场合献诗的人
senses.example: The poet laureate composed a piece for the coronation.
senses.exampleCN: 桂冠诗人为加冕典礼写了一首诗。
senses.why: When a court or a state wanted verse for its ceremonies, it kept a poet on hand, and that appointment turned the general word into an official title.
senses.whyCN: 当宫廷或国家需要为典礼准备诗句时，会长期供养一位诗人，这个任命就把普通名词变成了官方头衔。

senses.title: A person with a poet's sensibility
senses.titleCN: 有诗心的人；富于想象的人
senses.definition: someone who sees and describes ordinary things with unusual feeling or imagination
senses.definitionCN: 以不寻常的感受力或想象力观察、描述寻常事物的人
senses.example: He is a poet of the kitchen, turning cheap vegetables into something memorable.
senses.exampleCN: 他是厨房里的诗人，能把便宜蔬菜做成令人难忘的东西。
senses.why: If a poet is someone who makes ordinary language carry feeling, then anyone who does that in another craft can borrow the name.
senses.whyCN: 如果诗人就是让寻常语言承载情感的人，那么在任何别的行当里做到这一点的人，都可以借用这个称呼。

senses.title: A representative voice of a tradition
senses.titleCN: 某一诗歌传统的代表作者
senses.definition: a writer whose verse gives a language, an age or a movement its characteristic voice
senses.definitionCN: 其诗作赋予某个语言、时代或流派以鲜明声音的作者
senses.example: The poets of the Harlem Renaissance changed American literature.
senses.exampleCN: 哈莱姆文艺复兴的诗人们改变了美国文学。
senses.why: Because poems are made inside a shared language and a shared moment, the plural poets often names the group that gave a period its sound.
senses.whyCN: 因为诗总是在共同的语言与时代里写成，复数形式 poets 常用来指为一个时期定下声调的那一群人。

intro.en: Poet reaches English through Latin and French from a Greek word that first meant simply a maker, which is still the clearest clue to how the word thinks.
intro.cn: poet 经拉丁语、法语上溯到一个希腊词，那个词最初只表示「制作者」，这仍是理解这个词最清楚的线索。

items.en: The verb poiein meant to make or produce, and it was used of anything brought into being, not only verse.
items.cn: 动词 poiein 意为制作、产出，凡被做出来的东西都可以用它，并不专指诗句。

items.en: A poietes was a maker; calling the writer of verse the maker gradually made the noun mean poet.
items.cn: poietes 是「制作者」；把写诗的人称作制作者，这个名词就渐渐专指诗人。

items.en: Latin took poeta from Greek as a loan; the form is borrowed rather than native, so it does not follow ordinary Latin noun patterns.
items.cn: 拉丁语 poeta 借自希腊语，是外来借词而非本土词，所以词形不遵循一般拉丁名词的规律。

items.en: Old French poete carried the word into medieval literary life and passed it to English after the Norman period.
items.cn: 古法语 poete 把这个词带入中世纪的文学生活，并在诺曼时期之后传给英语。

items.en: English poet keeps the old idea that a poem is something made, while poet laureate adds an official, salaried role.
items.cn: 英语 poet 保留了「诗是被制作出来的东西」这一古老观念，而 poet laureate 又添上了带薪的官方身份。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words built on the same Greek making stem; the near-meaning group collects other names for people who write or recite.
note.cn: 形近组收同一希腊「制作」词干上的词；近义组收写诗、吟诵者的其他称呼。

entries.definition: Verse as a whole, the art this person practises.
entries.definitionCN: 诗歌总称；这个人所从事的这门艺术。

entries.definition: Written in verse, or full of the beauty associated with it.
entries.definitionCN: 以诗体写成的；富有诗意的。

entries.definition: A single piece of verse, countable where the collective noun is not.
entries.definitionCN: 单篇诗作，可数，与不可数的集合名词相对。

entries.definition: An old word for a woman who writes verse, now rarely used.
entries.definitionCN: 旧时指女诗人的词，今已少用。

entries.definition: An old word for a poet, especially a national or wandering one.
entries.definitionCN: 旧时指诗人，尤指民族诗人或行吟诗人。

entries.definition: A person who writes the words of songs.
entries.definitionCN: 为歌曲写词的人。

entries.definition: A person who produces books, stories or articles of any kind.
entries.definitionCN: 写书、写故事或写各类文章的人。

entries.definition: The person who originates a written work.
entries.definitionCN: 一部文字作品的创作者。

normalIntro.en: The word is a Greek making verb turned into a person, and the family around it keeps that same workshop image.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是把希腊语的「制作」动词变成一个人，围绕它的整族词都保留着同一幅作坊画面。

normal.en: Poet goes back to Greek poiein, to make, so the word calls a poem a thing made rather than a thing merely felt.
normal.cn: poet 上溯到希腊语 poiein（制作），所以这个词把诗看成做出来的东西，而不只是感受到的东西。

normal.en: The Greek agent ending -tes marks the doer, much as -er does in maker, so poietes is literally a maker.
normal.cn: 希腊语施事后缀 -tes 标示动作的执行者，作用近似 maker 里的 -er，所以 poietes 字面就是「制作者」。

normal.en: Poetry keeps the same stem but takes a collective ending: the art and its whole body of works, not one person.
normal.cn: poetry 保留同一词干却接了集合词尾：指这门艺术与全部作品，而不是一个人。

normal.en: Poetic adds the adjective ending -ic and describes the quality, which is why a sunset can be poetic with no verse in sight.
normal.cn: poetic 加形容词词尾 -ic，描述的是性质，所以一场日落即使没有半句诗也可以是诗意的。

normal.en: Latin poeta is a Greek loan, so no native Latin root should be invented to explain the shape.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 poeta 是希腊借词，不该为解释这个词形去编造拉丁本土词根。

abstract.en: A culture that names its poets makers is saying that language is material to be worked, not just air to be breathed.
abstract.cn: 一个把诗人称作「制作者」的文化是在说：语言是可以加工的材料，而不只是呼吸间的空气。

abstract.en: The same noun stretches from a person at a desk to a cook at a stove, because the act being named is shaping, not writing.
abstract.cn: 同一个名词从书桌前的人延伸到灶台前的厨师，因为被命名的是「塑形」这个动作，而不是写字。

abstract.en: Call someone a poet of a place and you grant that place a voice it did not have before.
abstract.cn: 把某人称作某地的诗人，等于承认那个地方从此有了过去没有的声音。

examples.en: The poet spent the morning revising a single stanza.
examples.cn: 这位诗人花了一上午修改一节诗。

examples.en: She is a poet of small-town life rather than of grand events.
examples.cn: 她是小镇生活的诗人，而不是写宏大事件的诗人。

examples.en: The poem was published without the poet's name.
examples.cn: 这首诗发表时没有署诗人的名字。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「泼伊特」——诗人把心里的东西一股脑泼在纸上，再一个字一个字拾起来排好。

root: 希腊语 poiein（制作）→ poietes（制作者、诗人）→ 拉丁语 poeta（借自希腊语）→ 古法语 poete → 英语 poet。

sensesIntro.en: The core is the maker of verse; from it come the appointed ceremonial voice, the borrowed praise for any imaginative worker, and the collective name for a school.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「诗句的制作者」；由此分出受任的典礼声音、借来形容任何富有想象力的行当的称呼，以及指一个流派的集合用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: someone bent over a desk at night, turning a surge of feeling into lines with a rhythm, crumpled paper at their feet.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人夜里伏在桌前，把翻涌的情绪改写成有节奏的句子，脚边堆着揉皱的纸。

branches.en: a writer at a desk and a writer on a ceremonial stage
branches.cn: 书桌前写作的人与典礼台上献诗的人

branches.en: a cook describing a bowl of soup as if it were a sonnet
branches.cn: 厨师把一碗汤说得像一首十四行诗

branches.en: a generation of writers giving an age its sound
branches.cn: 一代作家为一个时代定下声调

branches.en: one stanza revised until it finally stands
branches.cn: 一节诗被改到终于立住

branches.en: one name for an appointed role and for a shared tradition
branches.cn: 同一个称呼既指受任的角色，也指共享的传统

intro.en: A Greek verb of making supplies the root, a Greek agent ending makes it a person, and Latin and French pass the shape to English.
intro.cn: 一个表示制作的希腊动词提供词根，一个希腊施事后缀把它变成人，再经拉丁语与法语把词形传给英语。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

items.meaningCN: 希腊语施事后缀：做……的人

definition_zh: 推荐；建议；推荐信
definition_en: a suggestion that something is worth choosing; a letter praising a person; formal advice in a report
core_image: 教授在办公桌上写一封带签名的信
scene: 教授坐在办公桌旁，把写好的信装进信封，签上名字。 She wrote a letter of recommendation for her student.
sceneCN: 这里 recommendation 是「推荐信」（第 2 个义项：为某人说好话的书面材料）；句意为她为学生写了一封推荐信。画面里可留意：桌上的信纸、签好的名字。

senses.title: A suggestion to choose
senses.definition: a piece of advice that something is worth choosing or doing
senses.definitionCN: 认为某物值得选择或某事值得做的一条建议
senses.example: The committee made several recommendations.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会提出了若干建议。
senses.why: The noun turns the act of praising into a piece of advice that another person can follow.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词把称赞的行为变成一条他人可以照做的建议。

senses.title: A letter of praise
senses.definition: a written statement praising a person's qualities, usually for a job or a school
senses.definitionCN: 称赞某人品质的书面材料，通常用于求职或升学
senses.example: She wrote a letter of recommendation for her student.
senses.exampleCN: 她为学生写了一封推荐信。
senses.why: When praise is written down and signed, it becomes a document that travels without its author.
senses.whyCN: 当称赞被写下并签名，它就成了一份能脱离作者而流转的文件。

senses.title: Formal advice in a report
senses.definition: an official proposal made by a committee, an inspector, or a report
senses.definitionCN: 由委员会、检查员或报告提出的正式提议
senses.example: The report's recommendations were accepted by the board.
senses.exampleCN: 报告的建议被董事会采纳了。
senses.why: A committee that praises a policy in public is making a formal recommendation, and the word widened to official advice.
senses.whyCN: 委员会公开称赞某项政策，就是在提出正式建议，于是这个词扩展到官方意见。

intro.en: Recommendation is recommend plus the noun ending -ation: praise and advice turned into a thing one can hold.
intro.cn: recommendation 是 recommend 加名词词尾 -ation：称赞与建议变成了可以拿在手里的东西。

items.en: Mandare meant to hand over, the root behind the whole family.
items.cn: mandare 意为交出，是整个词族背后的词根。

items.en: Commendare joined praise to entrusting, giving both senses to the family.
items.cn: commendare 把称赞与托付结合，为词族带来两层含义。

items.en: The English verb recommend carries praise into a suggestion.
items.cn: 英语动词 recommend 把称赞带入建议。

items.en: The noun ending -ation marks the act or the result of recommending.
items.cn: 名词词尾 -ation 标记推荐的行为或结果。

items.en: Modern English uses the noun for personal advice, for letters, and for official reports.
items.cn: 现代英语用这个名词指个人建议、推荐信，以及官方报告。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers long nouns with the same ending; the near-meaning group gathers words for advice and support.
note.cn: 形近组收结尾相同的长名词；近义组收表建议与支持的词。

entries.definition: Formal praise for someone.
entries.definitionCN: 嘉奖；表扬。

entries.definition: Written material that proves or explains.
entries.definitionCN: 文件；文献记录。

entries.definition: A place to stay or a adjustment.
entries.definitionCN: 住宿；适应。

entries.definition: An idea put forward for consideration.
entries.definitionCN: 建议；提议。

entries.definition: Guidance about what to do.
entries.definitionCN: 劝告；建议。

entries.definition: A formal plan put forward.
entries.definitionCN: 提案。

entries.definition: Public support for something.
entries.definitionCN: 支持；背书。

normalIntro.en: The word is recommend plus ation: the act of praising becomes a suggestion, a letter, or a report.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是 recommend 加 ation：称赞的行为变成建议、信件或报告。

normal.en: Recommend plus -ation: the thing that is recommended, or the act itself.
normal.cn: recommend 加 -ation：被推荐的东西，或推荐这一行为。

normal.en: A letter of recommendation is a praise that can be carried away.
normal.cn: letter of recommendation 是一份可以带走的称赞。

normal.en: On the recommendation of means because someone advised it.
normal.cn: on the recommendation of 意为根据某人的建议。

normal.en: Make a recommendation is the formal way to say give advice.
normal.cn: make a recommendation 是「提出建议」的正式说法。

normal.en: The plural adds s: recommendations, with no change in the stem.
normal.cn: 复数加 s：recommendations，词干不变。

abstract.en: A recommendation is a piece of another person's judgment you are allowed to borrow.
abstract.cn: 一条建议，是你被允许借用的他人判断。

abstract.en: Written praise outlives the voice that spoke it.
abstract.cn: 写下的称赞，比说出它的声音活得更久。

abstract.en: Every recommendation carries the risk of being wrong in public.
abstract.cn: 每一条建议，都承担着公开出错的风险。

examples.en: The committee made several recommendations.
examples.cn: 委员会提出了若干建议。

examples.en: She wrote a letter of recommendation for her student.
examples.cn: 她为学生写了一封推荐信。

examples.en: The report's recommendations were accepted by the board.
examples.cn: 报告的建议被董事会采纳了。

dict_mnemonic.text: recommend（推荐）加 ation（行为、结果）：推荐这一行为，以及推荐所形成的东西——建议、推荐信。

root: recommend（推荐）+ 后缀 -ation（行为或结果）→ recommendation；recommend 源自拉丁 recommendare；同族有 recommendable。

sensesIntro.en: The core is praise made usable; the senses move from advice, to a signed letter, to a formal report.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「可用的称赞」；义项从建议，到签名信，再到正式报告。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a signed letter placed in an envelope on a desk.
core.cn: 核心意象：办公桌上，一封签好名的信被装进信封。

branches.en: a short list of good options
branches.cn: 一张写着好选项的短清单

branches.en: a letter sealed in an envelope
branches.cn: 封进信封的信

branches.en: a report read aloud at a meeting
branches.cn: 会上被朗读的报告

branches.en: advice spoken and advice written
branches.cn: 口头的建议与书面的建议

branches.en: a personal letter and an official report
branches.cn: 一封私人信件与一份官方报告

intro.en: The word adds a noun ending to the verb of praise, and the result names advice, a letter, and a report.
intro.cn: 这个词在表称赞的动词上加名词词尾，结果便指建议、信件与报告。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is mandare, to hand over; com- and re- shape the verb, and -ation names its result.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词根是 mandare（交出）；com- 与 re- 塑造动词，-ation 命名其结果。

definition_zh: 弯曲；弯道；屈服
definition_en: to make something curved, or a curve in a road
core_image: 柳枝被风压弯又弹回
scene: 风把河边的柳枝压了下去。 The wind bent the willow branches.
sceneCN: 这里 bend 是「使弯曲」（第 1 个义项：把直的东西压成弧形）；句意是风把柳枝吹弯了。

derivatives.zh: 由 bend 加 -er 构成，义为「弯曲者、狂欢」
由 bend 加 -y 构成，义为「易弯曲的」
由 un- 加 bend 构成，义为「弄直、放松」
由 bend 的过去分词转成的形容词，义为「弯的」

senses.title: To make something curved
senses.definition: to force something straight into a curve
senses.definitionCN: 把直的东西压成弧形
senses.example: The wind bent the willow branches.
senses.exampleCN: 风把柳枝吹弯了。
senses.why: This is the core sense, and it works for metal, wood and limbs.
senses.whyCN: 这是核心义，适用于金属、木头和肢体。

senses.title: A curve in a road
senses.definition: a place where a road turns
senses.definitionCN: 道路转弯的地方
senses.example: Slow down before the bend.
senses.exampleCN: 拐弯前要减速。
senses.why: The verb became a noun, naming the curved part itself.
senses.whyCN: 动词转作名词，用来指弯曲的那一段。

senses.title: To give in
senses.definition: to yield to pressure or rules
senses.definitionCN: 在压力或规则前让步
senses.example: He refused to bend to their demands.
senses.exampleCN: 他拒绝向他们的要求屈服。
senses.why: Something that bends under force gives up its straight shape.
senses.whyCN: 在力量下弯曲的东西，放弃了原本笔直的形状。

intro.en: Bend first meant to bend a bow, from an old Germanic verb.
intro.cn: bend 最初指把弓拉弯，来自古老的日耳曼语动词。

items.en: bendan meant to bend a bow.
items.cn: bendan 意为「把弓拉弯」。

items.en: the verb spread to any bending.
items.cn: 这个动词扩展到任何弯曲动作。

items.en: the noun named a curve in a road.
items.cn: 名词开始指道路的弯道。

items.en: bend also meant to submit.
items.cn: bend 也开始表示「屈服」。

items.en: bent is both past tense and adjective.
items.cn: 如今 bent 既是过去式，也是形容词。

note.en: The look-alike group differs by one vowel; the near-meaning group gives curve words.
note.cn: 形近组只差一个元音；近义组是表示弯曲的词。

entries.definition: a group of musicians
entries.definitionCN: 乐队

entries.definition: a close connection
entries.definitionCN: 纽带

entries.definition: curved out of shape
entries.definitionCN: 弯曲的

entries.definition: a line that turns smoothly
entries.definitionCN: 曲线

entries.definition: to change direction
entries.definitionCN: 转弯

entries.definition: to bend by turning
entries.definitionCN: 扭弯

normalIntro.en: Bend means to force a straight thing into a curve.
normalIntro.cn: bend 就是把直的东西逼成弧形。

normal.en: The past tense is bent.
normal.cn: 过去式是 bent。

normal.en: Bend down means lower your body.
normal.cn: bend down 指弯下身体。

normal.en: Bend the rules means loosen them a little.
normal.cn: bend the rules 指对规则稍作变通。

normal.en: A bend in the road is a curve.
normal.cn: a bend in the road 就是路的弯道。

normal.en: Bend to pressure means give in.
normal.cn: bend to pressure 指在压力下屈服。

abstract.en: See a willow branch pressed low by wind.
abstract.cn: 想象柳枝被风吹得低垂。

abstract.en: See a road curving around a hill.
abstract.cn: 想象道路绕山转弯。

abstract.en: See a metal bar folded by hands.
abstract.cn: 想象双手把金属条折弯。

examples.en: The wind bent the willow branches.
examples.cn: 风把柳枝吹弯了。

examples.en: Slow down before the bend.
examples.cn: 拐弯前要减速。

examples.en: He refused to bend to their demands.
examples.cn: 他拒绝向他们的要求屈服。

dict_mnemonic.text: bend 的 b 像弓身，把 d 压弯就成了弧形。

root: 古英语 bendan 本指给弓上弦、使弓弯曲，中古英语扩展为一切弯曲动作，十六世纪起作名词指弯道，十七世纪引申为屈服。

sensesIntro.en: A curved branch, a curved road and a yielding will all use bend.
sensesIntro.cn: 弯下的枝条、弯曲的道路、屈服的心志，都用 bend。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a willow branch pressed low by wind.
core.cn: 核心意象：被风吹得低垂的柳枝。

branches.en: bend the wire
branches.cn: 把铁丝弯弯

branches.en: bend down
branches.cn: 弯腰

branches.en: a sharp bend
branches.cn: 急弯

branches.en: bend to pressure
branches.cn: 屈服于压力

branches.en: bend the rules
branches.cn: 变通规则

intro.en: Bend takes -s, -ing and the irregular past bent.
intro.cn: bend 可加 -s、-ing，过去式是不规则的 bent。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin base; the word is Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: 这里没有拉丁词基，这个词来自日耳曼语。

definition_zh: 极其；非常；极端地
definition_en: to a very great degree; very; in an extreme way
core_image: 仪表指针一直冲到刻度尽头
scene: 这道题极其困难。 The problem is extremely difficult.
sceneCN: 这里 extremely 是「极其、非常」（第 1 个义项）；句意：这道题极其困难。

senses.title: To a very great degree
senses.definition: to a very great degree
senses.definitionCN: 达到非常大的程度
senses.example: The water is extremely cold.
senses.exampleCN: 水非常冷。
senses.why: The core sense is reaching the far end of a scale.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是达到刻度的最远端。

senses.title: At the limit
senses.definition: at the furthest limit of what is possible
senses.definitionCN: 达到可能范围的极限
senses.example: The machine is extremely sensitive.
senses.exampleCN: 这台机器极其敏感。
senses.why: A high degree becomes a point near the limit.
senses.whyCN: 高程度变成接近极限的点。

senses.title: In an extreme way
senses.definition: in a way that goes far beyond what is moderate
senses.definitionCN: 以远远超出温和范围的方式
senses.example: He reacted extremely to the criticism.
senses.exampleCN: 他对批评反应过激。
senses.why: Manner joins degree at the edge of a scale.
senses.whyCN: 方式与程度在刻度边缘结合。

intro.en: Extremely is extreme plus the adverb ending -ly.
intro.cn: extremely 由 extreme 加副词词尾 -ly 构成。

items.en: Extremus means farthest out.
items.cn: extremus 意为最靠外的。

items.en: The Latin form marks the highest degree.
items.cn: 拉丁语形式标记最高程度。

items.en: Extreme describes the far end.
items.cn: extreme 描述最远端。

items.en: The ending -ly turns it into a way or degree.
items.cn: 词尾 -ly 把它变成方式或程度副词。

items.en: Extremely is a common intensifier.
items.cn: 现代英语中 extremely 是常用强调词。

note.en: Extremely means very; externally means from outside.
note.cn: extremely 是极其，externally 则是从外部。

entries.definition: the furthest end of something
entries.definitionCN: 末端；极端

entries.definition: very great or severe
entries.definitionCN: 极端的

entries.definition: from or on the outside
entries.definitionCN: 从外部

entries.definition: to a high degree
entries.definitionCN: 非常

entries.definition: to a great degree
entries.definitionCN: 高度地；非常

entries.definition: extremely or very much
entries.definitionCN: 极大地

normalIntro.en: Extremely pushes an adjective or adverb to the far end.
normalIntro.cn: extremely 把形容词或副词推到最远端。

normal.en: The exam was extremely difficult.
normal.cn: 考试极其困难。

normal.en: This species is extremely rare.
normal.cn: 这个物种极其罕见。

normal.en: She was extremely pleased with the result.
normal.cn: 她对结果非常满意。

normal.en: The road is extremely narrow here.
normal.cn: 这里的路极其狭窄。

normal.en: He spoke extremely quietly.
normal.cn: 他说话声音非常轻。

abstract.en: Picture a needle pressed against the final mark.
abstract.cn: 想象指针被压到最后一个刻度。

abstract.en: Imagine a volume knob turned all the way up.
abstract.cn: 想象音量旋钮被拧到最大。

abstract.en: Think of a rope pulled to its tightest.
abstract.cn: 想象绳子被拉到最紧。

examples.en: The instructions are extremely clear.
examples.cn: 说明极其清楚。

examples.en: It is extremely unlikely that he will come.
examples.cn: 他来的可能性极小。

examples.en: She was extremely careful with the glass.
examples.cn: 她对那只玻璃杯非常小心。

dict_mnemonic.text: extreme 加副词后缀 -ly，表示「达到极端程度」，就是 extremely。

root: 由 extreme 加 -ly 构成，根源是拉丁语 extremus（最靠外的），核心义「达到极端的程度」。

sensesIntro.en: Extremely means to a very great degree, at the limit, or in an extreme way.
sensesIntro.cn: extremely 意为程度极高、达到极限，或以极端方式。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a needle at the final mark.
core.cn: 核心意象：停在最后刻度上的指针。

branches.en: The base sense is a very high degree.
