branches.cn: 高程度变成接近极限的点。

branches.en: Manner joins degree at the edge of a scale.
branches.cn: 方式与程度在刻度边缘结合。

branches.en: Very great and near the limit describe the same intensity.
branches.cn: 极大与接近极限描述同一种强度。

branches.en: Degree and manner can both be extreme.
branches.cn: 程度与方式都可能是极端的。

intro.en: Extremely is extreme plus -ly, and it belongs to the Latin exterus family.
intro.cn: extremely 由 extreme 加 -ly 构成，属于拉丁语 exterus 词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin extremus and exterus lie behind the word.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 extremus 与 exterus 是该词的来源。

items.exampleCN: 这名极端分子拒绝一切妥协。

latinEntries.example: Extra belongs to the same family.

definition_zh: 义务（良心或道德上必须履行的事）；法律义务（法令、合同或规章所规定的作为或不作为）；债务（必须偿付的款项或必须提供的给付）；人情债（受恩之后觉得应当回报的亏欠感）；约束力（誓约、承诺或规则对人的拘束力量）；受托职责（因担任职务而必须尽到的义务）；契据债券（以文书形式承认的付款义务）；被迫感（觉得别无选择、只能去做的心理压力）
definition_en: a binding requirement, whether moral, legal or contractual, that a person is bound to carry out or to pay
core_image: 一根绳子一头系在人的手腕上，另一头系在一张写满条款的纸上，风吹得纸响，绳子始终不松
scene: 公证处的窗口前，一位老人把一份发黄的借据摊在桌上，说当年借钱的人已经去世，他的儿子仍然每年送来利息。 The obligation had outlived the man who signed it.
sceneCN: 这里 obligation 指「按字据必须偿付的债务」（第 3 个义项：必须偿付的款项）；句意为这笔债比签字的人活得更久。可辨识物件：发黄的借据、窗口玻璃、红色印章、利息收条；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 义务；法律责任；债务；人情债；约束力；受托职责

forms.label: 形容词（受约束的；承蒙的）

senses.title: A duty felt in conscience
senses.definition: a duty that a person feels bound in conscience to perform, even when no one can compel it
senses.definitionCN: 一个人在良心上觉得必须履行、即使无人能强制也必须做的义务
senses.example: She felt an obligation to tell the family what she had seen.
senses.exampleCN: 她觉得有义务把自己看到的事告诉这家人。
senses.why: The Latin verb means to bind, so the word pictures a person tied to a task before any law appears.
senses.whyCN: 那个拉丁动词意为「捆绑」，所以这个词描绘的是在法律出现之前，一个人就已经被系在一件事上。

senses.title: A duty imposed by law or contract
senses.titleCN: 法律或合同规定的义务
senses.definition: a requirement that a statute, contract or official rule lays on a person and that can be enforced
senses.definitionCN: 由法令、合同或正式规章加于某人、并且可以被强制执行的作为或不作为要求
senses.example: The lease imposes an obligation to repair the roof by June.
senses.exampleCN: 租约规定了一项在六月前修好屋顶的义务。
senses.why: Once a court can enforce the bond, the image of a rope becomes a legal relation with a remedy.
senses.whyCN: 一旦法院可以强制执行这根绳子，捆绑的图景就变成带有救济手段的法律关系。

senses.title: A debt that must be paid
senses.definition: a sum of money or a service that one is bound to pay or provide to another
senses.definitionCN: 必须向他人偿付的款项，或必须向他人提供的给付
senses.example: The obligation had outlived the man who signed it.
senses.exampleCN: 这笔债比签字的人活得更久。
senses.why: Bonds are most often counted in money, so the general binding became a figure on a ledger.
senses.whyCN: 捆绑最常见于金钱，于是这种一般的约束就变成账本上的一个数字。

senses.title: A debt of gratitude
senses.definition: the sense of owing something back after receiving help or kindness that cannot be repaid in full
senses.definitionCN: 得到帮助或恩惠之后，觉得应当回报、却又无法完全还清的那种亏欠感
senses.example: He stayed to look after the old teacher out of a sense of obligation.
senses.exampleCN: 他留下来照顾那位老教师，是出于一份人情上的亏欠感。
senses.why: Kindness can bind as firmly as a contract, and English uses the same word for both ties.
senses.whyCN: 恩惠能像合同一样把人系住，英语对这两种束缚用了同一个词。

senses.title: The binding force of a promise
senses.titleCN: 誓约与规则具有的约束力
senses.definition: the force that a promise, oath or rule has in holding a person to a stated course of action
senses.definitionCN: 誓约、承诺或规则把一个人固定在既定做法上的那股力量
senses.example: The oath carried an obligation that he could not easily set aside.
senses.exampleCN: 那个誓约带着一种约束力，他无法轻易搁下。
senses.why: Here the noun names not the task but the pull that keeps a person from walking away.
senses.whyCN: 这里名词指的不是任务，而是不让一个人走开的那股拉力。

senses.title: Duties attached to a trust or office
senses.titleCN: 受托或任职所带来的职责
senses.definition: the specific duties that a person must perform because of a post or a trust accepted
senses.definitionCN: 因担任某个职位或接受某项托付而必须履行的具体职责
senses.example: A trustee's obligations include keeping accounts open to inspection.
senses.exampleCN: 受托人的职责包括保存可供查阅的账目。
senses.why: A post adds its own set, so the general bond becomes a list that other people can check.
senses.whyCN: 一个职位自带一整套要求，于是笼统的捆绑变成别人可以核对的清单。

senses.title: A sealed bond or written undertaking
senses.titleCN: 契据形式的债券与承诺书
senses.definition: in law, a written document under seal by which a person binds himself to pay a sum or to perform an act
senses.definitionCN: 在法律上指加盖印章的文书，当事人在其中承诺付款或履行某项行为
senses.example: The estate settled the obligation recorded in the bond.
senses.exampleCN: 遗产管理人清偿了债券上记载的那笔债务。
senses.why: The word once named the paper itself, because the paper was the thing that did the binding.
senses.whyCN: 这个词曾经直接指那张纸，因为起捆绑作用的就是那张纸。

senses.title: The felt pressure of having no choice
senses.definition: the state of feeling compelled to act, whether or not one agrees with the act
senses.definitionCN: 觉得不得不做某事的状态，不论自己是否认同这件事
senses.example: He signed the form under obligation, not out of any belief in the scheme.
senses.exampleCN: 他在被迫的情况下签了表格，并不是因为相信这个方案。
senses.why: When the tie is felt from the inside, the noun describes a pressure rather than a duty owed.
senses.whyCN: 当这根绳子从内部被感受到时，这个名词描述的是压力，而不是欠下的义务。

intro.en: Obligation comes from Latin obligare 'to bind, tie up', built on ob- 'towards, against' and ligare 'to bind'. The noun obligatio passed through Old French into English, keeping both the moral and the legal sense.
intro.cn: obligation 来自拉丁 obligare「捆绑、约束」，由 ob-「朝向、对着」与 ligare「绑」构成。名词 obligatio 经古法语进入英语，同时保留了道德与法律两层意思。

items.en: Ligare meant 'to bind, tie'. It also gives ligament and ligature, where the same root names things that fasten; its deeper origin is not established, so any earlier form offered for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: ligare 意为「绑、系」。它同样给出 ligament 与 ligature，同一个词根在两词中指起固定作用的东西；其更深的来源未获证明，凡为其提出的更早形式都属重构形式。

items.en: Ob- 'towards, against' plus ligare formed obligare, 'to bind towards someone', hence to put a person under a duty. The prefix marks the direction of the tie, not its strength.
items.cn: ob-「朝向、对着」加 ligare 构成 obligare，意为「朝某人绑过去」，引申为使某人负上义务。前缀标的是捆绑的方向，而不是力度。

items.en: The noun obligatio named both the act of binding and the bond itself; Roman law used it for a tie that could be enforced by an action.
items.cn: 名词 obligatio 既指捆绑的动作，也指束缚本身；罗马法用它指可以通过诉讼强制执行的约束关系。

items.en: Old French obligation carried the moral sense of a duty and the legal sense of a bond, and English adopted it in the fourteenth century.
items.cn: 古法语 obligation 兼有道德义务与法律债券两层意思，英语在十四世纪借入。

items.en: English law kept the written-bond sense, and the everyday moral sense grew beside it; obligation to and under an obligation are the modern frames that separate them.
items.cn: 英国法保留了文书债券的义项，日常的道德义在旁边生长；后接表示对象的介词，与「负有义务」这一固定说法，正是今天区分两者的框架。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin of ligare and the English date): the link with religion is real but semantic only, since religio is generally explained as re- plus ligare in the sense of binding fast, while ally and alliance come from ad- plus ligare with a different prefix and a different sense, and obligation shares the root with religion without sharing any meaning.
items.cn: 来源不确定（ligare 的更深来源与英语首见年代）：与 religion 的联系确实存在，但只在词根层面，因为 religio 一般被解释为 re- 加 ligare、取「紧紧绑住」之意，而 ally 与 alliance 则出自 ad- 加 ligare，前缀不同、语义也不同；obligation 与 religion 共享词根，却没有任何义项上的关系。

note.en: Group one holds words from the same binding root, each with a different prefix or ending, so the meanings diverge sharply; group two holds nouns that also put a person under a demand, with a different source for that demand.
note.cn: 第一组同出「绑」这个词根，但前缀或词尾各不相同，语义因此分得很开；第二组是同样把人置于某种要求之下的名词，只是要求的来源不同。

entries.definition: The verb behind the noun: to bind someone by law, by duty or by a favour done, and in polite use simply to do someone a kindness.
entries.definitionCN: 这个名词背后的动词：以法律、义务或恩惠把人绑住；在客套用法中则只表示帮某人一个忙。

entries.definition: Made from the noun with the ending -ory, meaning required rather than optional; it describes the requirement, not the person under it.
entries.definitionCN: 由这个名词加表示「具有……性质的」词尾构成，意为强制的而非可选的；它描述要求本身，而不是被要求的人。

entries.definition: Built on ligare with a different stem: it names the band that binds a joint, and the binding here is physical.
entries.definitionCN: 以 ligare 加另一个词干构成：它指把关节绑住的韧带，这里的捆绑是身体上的。

entries.definition: Generally explained as re- plus ligare, 'to bind fast'; it shares the root but has no sense relation to a duty or a debt.
entries.definitionCN: 一般解释为 re- 加 ligare「紧紧绑住」；它与本词共享词根，却与义务、债务没有任何义项关系。

entries.definition: From ad- 'to' plus ligare, 'to bind to one side'; it names a partner joined by agreement, and the prefix, not the root, does the work.
entries.definitionCN: 出自 ad-「向」加 ligare「绑到一边」；它指因约定而结合的伙伴，起作用的是前缀而不是词根。

entries.definition: What a person owes by law, by office or by conscience; duty is the content, while obligation stresses the tie that holds the person to it.
entries.definitionCN: 一个人依法、依职或依良知所欠之事；义务是内容，而 obligation 强调把人系在这件事上的那根绳子。

entries.definition: A promise or engagement a person has taken on, usually by choice; obligation can be imposed without consent.
entries.definitionCN: 一个人通常自愿承担下来的承诺或投入；obligation 则可以在未经同意时被加于身上。

entries.definition: Legal responsibility for a debt or damage, measured in money; it is the narrow financial end of obligation.
entries.definitionCN: 对债务或损害承担的法律责任，以金钱衡量；它是 obligation 最窄的财务一端。

entries.definition: A condition that must be met, often written into a rule or a contract; it names the condition, not the bond that makes it binding.
entries.definitionCN: 必须满足的条件，常写入规则或合同；它指条件本身，而不是使其具有约束力的那根绳子。

entries.definition: The state of having to answer for something; it looks at who must explain, while obligation looks at what binds them to act.
entries.definitionCN: 必须为某事作出交代的状态；它着眼的是该由谁解释，而 obligation 着眼的是把人绑向行动的东西。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Latin verb of binding, its prefix, the real family, the real phrases, and the relatives that share the root but carry different prefixes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁「捆绑」动词、它的前缀、真实的词族、真实的搭配，以及共享词根却带不同前缀的亲戚。

normal.en: Ob- means towards and ligare means to bind, so an obligation is a rope tied towards a task.
normal.cn: ob- 意为「朝向」，ligare 意为「绑」，所以义务就是一根朝某件事绑过去的绳子。

normal.en: The family runs oblige, obliged, obliging, obligatory, obligatorily and obligee.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 oblige、obliged、obliging、obligatory、obligatorily 与 obligee。

normal.en: Fixed phrases show the frames: a legal obligation, under an obligation to, fulfil an obligation, without obligation.
normal.cn: 固定搭配显出常用框架：法律义务、有义务去做、履行义务、不附带义务。

normal.en: The same root appears with other prefixes: a ligament binds a joint, religion binds fast, and an ally is bound to one side.
normal.cn: 同一个词根配上别的前缀：ligament 绑住关节，religion 取「紧紧绑住」之意，ally 则是被绑到一边的伙伴。

normal.en: Obligation is what ties a person to act; responsibility is what a person must answer for afterwards.
normal.cn: obligation 是把人绑向行动的东西，responsibility 则是事后必须为之作答的东西。

abstract.en: Picture a rope running from a wrist to a sheet of clauses, slack enough to move but never loose enough to slip off.
abstract.cn: 想象一根绳子从手腕连到一页条款上，松到可以活动，却绝不会松脱。

abstract.en: Picture a signed card in a coat pocket that grows heavier with every year it is carried.
abstract.cn: 想象外套口袋里一张签过字的卡片，带得越久就越沉。

abstract.en: Picture two posts with a rope stretched between them, so that walking past means ducking under it.
abstract.cn: 想象两根柱子之间拉着一根绳，走过那里就得低头钻过去。

examples.en: Members are under an obligation to declare any outside income.
examples.cn: 成员有义务申报任何外部收入。

examples.en: He helped her move, and she now feels an obligation to return the favour.
examples.cn: 他帮她搬了家，她现在觉得欠着一份应当回报的人情。

examples.en: The bond is an obligation enforceable in court.
examples.cn: 这张债券是一项可以在法院强制执行的义务。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「朝向 + 绑」——把你朝某件事绑过去的那根绳子，就是义务；绳子换成钱，就是债务

root: 拉丁 obligare「捆绑、约束」= ob-（朝向、对着）+ ligare「绑」；名词 obligatio 经古法语 obligation 进入英语。同根词有 ligament、ligature、religion（re- 加 ligare，紧紧绑住）、ally 与 alliance（ad- 加 ligare）；前缀不同，语义各异。ligare 的更深来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one rope: conscience ties it, law tightens it, money counts it, gratitude feels it, the noun then names the force itself, lists the duties of a post, records it as a sealed bond, and finally describes the pressure of being pulled from inside.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿着同一根绳子展开：良心先把它系上，法律把它收紧，金钱把它算成数目，感恩从内部感到它；随后名词指这股力量本身、列出职位的职责、把它记成盖章的债券，最后描述被从内部拉扯的压力。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a rope from a wrist to a page of clauses, slack enough to move but never loose enough to slip off.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根从手腕连到条款纸页的绳子，松到可以活动，却绝不会松脱。

branches.en: INNER TIE AND ITS FORCE: the duty felt and the binding power that holds a person are one rope seen as content and as strength.
branches.cn: 内在的系与它的力：被感受到的义务与把人固定的力量，是同一根绳子作为内容与作为力度的一面。

branches.en: PAPER AND LAW: a statute and a sealed bond are two ways of writing the tie down.
branches.cn: 纸与法：法令与盖章债券，是把这根绳子写下来的两种方式。

branches.en: TWO KINDS OF DEBT: money can be counted and repaid, while gratitude cannot.
branches.cn: 两种债：钱可以算清也可以还清，恩情却不行。

branches.en: THE POST: an office supplies its own list of duties, which other people can inspect.
branches.cn: 职位：一个岗位自带一份职责清单，别人可以逐项核对。

branches.en: PULLED FROM INSIDE: when the rope is felt rather than owed, the word names compulsion.
branches.cn: 从内部被拉：当绳子是被感受到而不是被欠下时，这个词指的就是被迫。

intro.en: Obligation reads as a prefix of direction, a root meaning to bind, and a noun ending that names the resulting state or instrument.
intro.cn: obligation 可以读成表示方向的前缀、意为「绑」的词根，以及指称由此形成的状态或文书的名称词尾。

latinIntro.en: The root ligare also gives ligament, ligature, religion, ally and alliance; ob- marks direction towards, while re- and ad- give those other words their different senses.
latinIntro.cn: 词根 ligare 还给出 ligament、ligature、religion、ally 与 alliance；ob- 标出「朝向」，re- 与 ad- 则让其余各词各有不同语义。

items.example: The prefix shows the direction in which the binding is done.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀指出捆绑是朝哪个方向做的。

items.example: The root supplies the physical picture of a rope.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根提供绳子的具体形象。

items.meaning: to bind towards; to put under a duty
items.example: The verb turns a literal rope into a duty owed to a person.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词把字面的绳子变成对某人的义务。

items.example: The Latin noun names both the act and the tie it creates.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁名词既指动作，也指动作造成的束缚。

items.meaning: a duty; a debt; a bond
items.example: The obligation had outlived the man who signed it.
items.exampleCN: 这笔债比签字的人活得更久。

items.example: Attendance at the safety briefing is obligatory.
items.exampleCN: 参加安全说明会是强制性的。

items.meaning: to bind by duty; to do a kindness
items.example: The rules oblige the carrier to inspect every crate.
items.exampleCN: 规则要求承运方检查每一个板条箱。

items.meaning: the person to whom a bond is owed
items.example: The obligee may demand payment on the stated date.
items.exampleCN: 债权人可以在约定日期要求付款。

definition_zh: 调整；调节；适应；校准；整理；校正
definition_en: to change something slightly so that it fits better, to get used to a new situation, or to set a device to a standard
core_image: 把歪掉的画框扶正，让它与墙面刚好平行
scene: 新装的门关上时总蹭到地板，木匠蹲下来查看合页。 He turned the screw to adjust the hinge.
sceneCN: 这里 adjust 是「校准、调校」（第 3 个义项：把部件或仪器调到正确位置）；句意为他转动螺丝来调节合页。

pos.zh: 及物动词：调整、调节；校准；整理（衣饰）；校正
不及物动词：适应（新环境）

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词后缀 -ment 构成，义为「调整；调节；适应」
由本词加形容词后缀 -able 构成，义为「可调节的」
由本词加名词后缀 -er 构成，义为「调节器；理赔员」
由前缀 re- 加本词构成，义为「重新调整；再适应」

senses.title: To change something slightly
senses.definition: to change something a little, especially so that it works better or fits a situation
senses.definitionCN: 对某物作小幅改动，尤指使其运转更好或更适应情况
senses.example: You can adjust the height of the chair with this lever.
senses.exampleCN: 你可以用这个把手调整椅子的高度。
senses.why: Late Latin adiustare meant 'to bring to the right measure': the change is small because the thing is only slightly off and must be set right again.
senses.whyCN: 晚期拉丁语 adiustare 意为「使达到正确的尺度」：改动之所以小，是因为物件只偏了一点，把它拨回正确的位置即可。

senses.title: To get used to a new situation
senses.definition: to become familiar with a new place, condition or way of life and act comfortably in it
senses.definitionCN: 逐渐熟悉新的地点、状况或生活方式，并在其中自如行事
senses.example: It took her a month to adjust to the colder climate.
senses.exampleCN: 她花了一个月才适应更冷的气候。
senses.why: If the conditions have shifted, the person must be brought back into line with them; adjusting to something is the same straightening, applied to oneself.
senses.whyCN: 条件变了，人就得重新与它对齐；adjust to 说的是同一件「扶正」的事，只是对象换成了自己。

senses.title: To set an instrument to a standard
senses.definition: to set a device, instrument or machine so that it works correctly or shows a true value
senses.definitionCN: 把装置、仪器或机器调到正确运转或显示真实值的位置
senses.example: The technician adjusted the telescope before the observation began.
senses.exampleCN: 观测开始前，技师校准了望远镜。
senses.why: A device is right only when its reading matches the standard, so adjusting it is making it exactly right again, which is the original force of iustus 'correct'.
senses.whyCN: 仪器读数与标准吻合才算对，所以 adjust 就是让它重新精确地对上，这正是 iustus「正确」的本义。

senses.title: To tidy one's clothes or appearance
senses.definition: to move or arrange part of your clothing or appearance so that it sits neatly
senses.definitionCN: 把衣着或仪容的某部分弄整齐
senses.example: She adjusted her scarf before stepping into the interview room.
senses.exampleCN: 她进面试室前整了整围巾。
senses.why: A collar out of place is a small thing set right; the same verb covers straightening a tie and straightening a machine.
senses.whyCN: 领子歪了也是把一件小事扶正；同一个动词既管整理领带，也管调校机器。

senses.title: To correct a figure for a factor
senses.titleCN: 校正；扣除某因素的影响
senses.definition: to change a figure or result so that the effect of a particular factor is taken into account
senses.definitionCN: 改动数字或结果，以便把某一因素的影响计算在内
senses.example: The figures were adjusted for inflation before comparison.
senses.exampleCN: 这些数字在比较前已按通货膨胀作了校正。
senses.why: Here the correction happens on paper: the raw number is brought into line with a fair standard so that two sets of figures can be compared.
senses.whyCN: 这里的修正在纸面上完成：把原始数字拉到公平的标准线上，两组数字才能比较，所以也用同一个词。

intro.en: Adjust comes from Latin iustus 'right, just' through a verb meaning 'to bring to the right measure', and reached English from Old French.
intro.cn: adjust 出自拉丁语 iustus「正确的、公正的」，经由一个表示「使达到正确尺度」的动词，再从古法语进入英语。

items.en: Ius meant 'right, law', and the adjective iustus 'just, correct' grew from it.
items.cn: ius 意为「权利、法」，形容词 iustus「公正的、正确的」由它而来。

items.en: Iustus meant 'just, right, correct', and it still survives in the English words just and justice.
items.cn: iustus 意为「公正的、正确的」，英语的 just 与 justice 仍保留着它。

items.en: Ad- 'to' plus iustus formed adiustare, generally explained as 'to bring to the right measure, set right'.
items.cn: ad-「朝向」加 iustus 构成 adiustare，一般认为意为「使达到正确的尺度、把……弄正」。

items.en: Old French ajuster meant 'to arrange, fit, join', and it carried the verb into Middle English.
items.cn: 古法语 ajuster 意为「安排、使合适、接合」，它把这个动词带进中古英语。

items.en: The verb is recorded from the late fourteenth century, first for arranging and settling affairs and later for setting instruments; the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 这个动词自十四世纪末有记录，先指安排与了结事务，后来才用于调校仪器；确切首见年代不确定。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the word's own family; the near-meaning group holds words for adapting, changing and setting instruments, which differ in scope.
note.cn: 形近组收本词自己的词族；近义组收表示适应、改动与调校的词，彼此范围不同。

entries.definition: A small change made so that something works or fits better.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「调整、调节」，由本词加后缀 -ment 构成。

entries.definition: Built so that its position or setting can be changed.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「可调节的」，由本词加后缀 -able 构成。

entries.definition: A person or device that adjusts, especially one who settles insurance claims.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「调节器、理赔员」，由本词加后缀 -er 构成。

entries.definition: To adjust again after a first change or a period of use.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「重新调整、再适应」，由前缀 re- 加本词构成。

entries.definition: To change something, or oneself, so as to suit new conditions; often a deeper change than adjust.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「使适应、改编」，改动往往比 adjust 更深，常指为适合新条件而改造。

entries.definition: To change something in form or detail, without the idea of fitting a standard.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「修改、改动」，只强调改变形式或细节，不含「对准标准」的意思。

entries.definition: To mark or correct an instrument against a known standard; narrower and more technical than adjust.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「校准、标定」，专指按已知标准对仪器进行标定，比 adjust 更专门。

entries.definition: To set a musical instrument or an engine to the right pitch or setting.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「调音、调校」，多用于乐器或发动机，调的是音高或运转状态。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin root iustus 'right' and the fixed patterns adjust to and adjust for.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的记忆钩子使用真实的拉丁词根 iustus「正确的」，以及 adjust to 与 adjust for 两个固定结构。

normal.en: Iustus is 'right': to adjust is to put something back to right.
normal.cn: iustus 是「正确的」：adjust 就是把某物重新弄正。

normal.en: The same root survives in just and justice, both about what is right.
normal.cn: 同一词根还留在 just 与 justice 里，两者讲的都是「正当」。

normal.en: Adjust to is for people and new conditions; adjust for is for figures and hidden factors.
normal.cn: adjust to 接人和新环境，adjust for 接数字和隐藏因素。

normal.en: Adjustable means the thing is built to be set right again and again.
normal.cn: adjustable 说明这件东西本来就被设计成可以反复调正的。

normal.en: An adjuster is the person who settles an insurance claim, literally setting the figure right.
normal.cn: adjuster 是处理保险理赔的人，字面上就是把那个数目「弄正」的人。

abstract.en: Picture a crooked frame pushed straight with one thumb until its edges run level with the wall.
abstract.cn: 想象用一根拇指把歪掉的画框推正，直到边缘与墙面平行。

abstract.en: The push is always small: adjust never means rebuild, only set right what has slipped.
abstract.cn: 那一下推动总是很轻：adjust 从不表示重造，只表示把滑开的部分拨回去。

abstract.en: A person can be the crooked frame: when the world shifts, the same small straightening happens inside.
abstract.cn: 人也可以是那只歪画框：世界一变，同样一次小幅的扶正就发生在自己身上。

examples.en: You can adjust the height of the chair with this lever.
examples.cn: 你可以用这个把手调整椅子的高度。

examples.en: It took her a month to adjust to the colder climate.
examples.cn: 她花了一个月才适应更冷的气候。

examples.en: The figures were adjusted for inflation before comparison.
examples.cn: 这些数字在比较前已按通货膨胀作了校正。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿贾斯特」——阿贾把歪画框一推，正好齐边：调整、校准。

root: 拉丁语 adiustare「使达到正确尺度」，由 ad-「朝向」+ iustus「正确的、公正的」构成，后者出自 ius「权利、法」；经古法语 ajuster 进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: The five senses of adjust all describe a small correction: an object, a person, an instrument, a piece of clothing, or a set of figures is brought back into line.
sensesIntro.cn: adjust 的五个义项都描述一次小幅校正：物件、人、仪器、衣饰或一组数字被重新拉回到该在的位置。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a crooked picture frame pushed straight until its edges line up with the wall.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只歪掉的画框被推正，边缘与墙面齐平。

branches.en: OBJECT: the chair or the frame is only a little off, so a small turn sets it right.
branches.cn: 物件线：椅子或画框只偏了一点，稍微一转就正了。

branches.en: PERSON: a newcomer is brought back into line with an unfamiliar place.
branches.cn: 人线：新来的人被重新调整到与陌生环境一致的线上。

branches.en: INSTRUMENT: a device is adjusted until its reading matches the standard.
branches.cn: 仪器线：装置被调到读数与标准吻合。

branches.en: APPEARANCE: a scarf or a tie is set neatly, the smallest version of the same act.
branches.cn: 仪容线：围巾或领带被弄整齐，是同一动作最小的版本。

branches.en: FIGURE: a number is corrected on paper so that a comparison becomes fair.
branches.cn: 数字线：数字在纸面上被校正，比较才变得公平。

intro.en: Adjust is a Latin prefix plus iustus 'right', routed through Old French; English adds common endings for the family.
intro.cn: adjust 由拉丁语前缀加 iustus「正确的」构成，经古法语转来，英语再用常见词尾扩展出词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin ius, iustus and adiustare are recorded; the Old French verb is also attested, so nothing here is invented.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 ius、iustus 与 adiustare 均有记录，古法语动词也有文献可查，这里没有虚构形式。

items.example: It adds the idea of moving towards a state.
items.exampleCN: 它加上「朝某个状态移动」的意思。

items.example: Ius is the deepest recorded noun of the family.
items.exampleCN: ius 是这个词族中可考的最早名词。

items.example: Iustus supplies the sense of rightness in adjust.
items.exampleCN: iustus 为 adjust 提供「正确」这层意思。

items.meaning: to bring to the right measure
items.example: It is the verb behind the English word.
items.exampleCN: 它是英语这个词背后的拉丁动词。

items.example: Old French shaped the word before English borrowed it.
items.exampleCN: 英语借入之前，古法语已把这个词塑造成形。

latinEntries.meaning: to bring to the right measure

derivatives.zh: 由本词加后缀 -ment 构成，义为「调整；适应」
由本词加后缀 -able 构成，义为「可调节的」
由前缀 re- 加本词构成，义为「重新调整」

definition_zh: 分发；分布；配送
definition_en: to give things out to people, or to spread them over an area
core_image: 一叠传单从怀里抽出，一张张递到不同的手上
scene: 门口排起了队，他把传单一张张递过去。 Volunteers distribute blankets to every family.
sceneCN: 这里 distribute 指「分发」（第 1 个义项：把东西分给各人）；句意是志愿者把毯子分给每一家。

senses.title: To give a share to each
senses.definition: to give part of something to each person or place
senses.definitionCN: 把东西的一部分给到每个人或每处
senses.example: They distributed the blankets at the gate.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在大门口分发毯子。
senses.why: A pile becomes fair only when it is handed out.
senses.whyCN: 一堆东西只有分到手上，才谈得上公平。

senses.title: To spread across an area
senses.definition: to spread something over an area or among groups
senses.definitionCN: 把东西散在一整片地方或人群里
senses.example: The seeds are distributed by the wind.
senses.exampleCN: 种子靠风散开。
senses.why: What is scattered stops belonging to one place.
senses.whyCN: 散开的东西，就不再只属于一处。

intro.en: Distribute comes from Latin distribuere, to deal out, from dis-, apart, and tribuere, to assign.
intro.cn: distribute 来自拉丁语 distribuere（分派），由 dis-（分开）与 tribuere（分给）构成。

items.en: Tribuere meant to assign or grant a share.
items.cn: tribuere 指分派或给予一份。

items.en: Dis- sent the shares to different hands.
items.cn: dis- 把各份送到不同的人手里。

items.en: Distribuere covered both giving out and spreading.
items.cn: distribuere 既指分发，也指铺开。

items.en: English used it for sharing goods among people.
items.cn: 英语借入时指把物品分给众人。

items.en: The sense of spreading over land grew common.
items.cn: 后来「散布在土地上」的用法普遍起来。

items.en: Today a company distributes films as well as parcels.
items.cn: 今天公司既配送包裹，也发行影片。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the tribuere stem, while the meaning group gathers other ways of giving out.
note.cn: 形近组共享 tribuere 这段词干，近义组则是几种把东西给出去的说法。

entries.definition: the act of giving out or spreading
entries.definitionCN: 分发或散布的行为

entries.definition: a person or firm that passes goods on
entries.definitionCN: 把货物转送出去的经销商

entries.definition: to give a share to a common pool
entries.definitionCN: 为共同的一份出一份力

entries.definition: to give out for a stated purpose
entries.definitionCN: 按规定用途分给

entries.definition: to cover a wider and wider area
entries.definitionCN: 铺开并覆盖更大范围

entries.definition: to carry goods to a place
entries.definitionCN: 把货物送到某处

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a stack of papers and end with seeds carried far by wind.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从一叠纸开始，落到被风带得很远的种子。

normal.en: Dis- plus tribute: each share goes to a different hand.
normal.cn: dis 加 tribute，每一份都送到不同的人手里。

normal.en: Helpers distributed water along the whole route.
normal.cn: 帮手沿整条路线分发饮水。

normal.en: The weight must be distributed over both legs.
normal.cn: 重量要分到两条腿上。

normal.en: This plant is distributed across the whole south.
normal.cn: 这种植物遍布整个南方。

normal.en: The firm distributes its goods by rail.
normal.cn: 这家公司用铁路配送货物。

abstract.en: Picture a stack of leaflets leaving one hand for many.
abstract.cn: 想象一叠传单从一只手里分到许多手上。

abstract.en: Picture seeds let go and carried off in all directions.
abstract.cn: 想象种子被放开，朝四面散去。

abstract.en: Picture a map dotted with the same mark again and again.
abstract.cn: 想象一张地图上同一个标记点了一次又一次。

examples.en: The teacher distributed the papers at the door.
examples.cn: 老师在门口把试卷发下去。

examples.en: Rainfall is distributed evenly across the region.
examples.cn: 降雨均匀分布在整个地区。

examples.en: The charity distributes meals every evening.
examples.cn: 这家慈善机构每天晚上分发饭菜。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 distribute 记成「分开给」：dis 表示分开，tribute 表示给，分开来给，就是分发；东西分到各处，也就成了分布。

root: 源自拉丁语 distribuere，由 dis-（分开）与 tribuere（分给、分派）组成。本义是把一份份东西分给不同的人，后来也指把事物铺展到一片地方，于是兼有「分发」与「分布」两层意思。

sensesIntro.en: From a share placed in each hand to a pattern of marks spread across a map.
sensesIntro.cn: 从一份份放进各人手里，到散在整张地图上的标记。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stack of leaflets leaving one hand and arriving in many.
core.cn: 核心意象：一叠传单从一只手里离开，落到许多只手上。

branches.en: The first sense is the act of handing out shares.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是把一份份递出去的动作。

branches.en: The second sense is the pattern left after spreading.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是散开之后留下的样子。

branches.en: Both senses start with one source and end in many places.
branches.cn: 两个义项都从一处出发，落到许多地方。

branches.en: Both can be even or badly uneven.
branches.cn: 两个义项都可能是均匀的，也可能很不均。

branches.en: Only the second sense can be drawn on a map.
branches.cn: 只有第二个义项能画在地图上。

intro.en: Distribute belongs to the tribuere family, where Latin tribuere, to assign, meets several prefixes.
intro.cn: distribute 属于 tribuere 一族，中心是拉丁语 tribuere（分给），前后接上不同前缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin tribuere, to assign, gives tribute and contribute; dis- spreads the shares apart.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 tribuere（分给）给出 tribute 与 contribute，前缀 dis- 把各份分送开来。

items.meaning: to hand out shares to many
the act or pattern of giving out
items.example: The distribution of rainfall is uneven.
A local distributor handles the stock.
The job has a distributive side.
items.exampleCN: 这份工作有分配的一面。
这个方案重新分配土地。

items.meaning: to give into a common pool
to assign a cause or quality
items.example: She attributes her win to luck.

items.meaning: a gift given to show respect
items.example: The song is a tribute to her teacher.
items.exampleCN: 这首歌是献给老师的敬意。

definition_zh: 退休；退休生活；退役
definition_en: the state of having stopped work, usually because of age
core_image: 办公桌上收拾干净的相框，窗外是缓慢的午后阳光
scene: 退休以后，他搬到了海边的小城，开始学画画。 After retirement, he moved to a small seaside town and began to learn painting.
sceneCN: 这里 retirement 是「退休」（第 1 个义项：因年龄原因停止工作后的状态）；句意：退休以后，他搬到了海边的小城，开始学画画。

senses.title: Leaving work
senses.definition: the act of stopping work because of age
senses.definitionCN: 因年龄原因停止工作的行为
senses.example: He chose early retirement at fifty-five.
senses.exampleCN: 他在五十五岁选择了提前退休。
senses.why: The noun names the state produced by the verb retire.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词指动词 retire 所产生的状态。

senses.title: The years after work
senses.definition: the period of life after leaving a job
senses.definitionCN: 离开工作之后的人生阶段
senses.example: She enjoys a busy retirement with her grandchildren.
senses.exampleCN: 她的退休生活很忙碌，常和孙辈在一起。
senses.why: A state that lasts for years becomes a stage of life.
senses.whyCN: 持续多年的状态就成为一个生活阶段。

senses.title: Leaving a sport
senses.definition: the end of a sports career
senses.definitionCN: 运动生涯的结束
senses.example: His retirement from tennis surprised his fans.
senses.exampleCN: 他从网坛退役让球迷感到意外。
senses.why: Athletes also step back from a long career, as workers do.
senses.whyCN: 运动员也像工作者一样，从长期生涯中退下来。

intro.en: Retirement is retire plus -ment, from French retirer, to draw back.
intro.cn: retirement 是 retire 加 -ment，源自法语 retirer（退回）。

items.en: Retirer means to draw back.
items.cn: retirer 意为退回。

items.en: Retire first means withdraw to a private place.
items.cn: retire 最初指退到私密之处。

items.en: Retirement comes to mean leaving work at a certain age.
items.cn: retirement 逐渐指到一定年龄离开工作。

items.en: It also names the years after work.
items.cn: 它也指工作之后的岁月。

items.en: Athletes speak of retirement from sport.
items.cn: 运动员也说从运动中退役。

note.en: Retirement is the noun of retire, close to resignation and withdrawal.
note.cn: retirement 是 retire 的名词，与辞职、退出相近。

entries.definition: to stop working
entries.definitionCN: 退休

entries.definition: no longer working
entries.definitionCN: 退休的

entries.definition: a retired person
entries.definitionCN: 退休者

entries.definition: the act of officially leaving a job
entries.definitionCN: 辞职

entries.definition: the act of moving back
entries.definitionCN: 退出

entries.definition: money paid after retirement
entries.definitionCN: 养老金

normalIntro.en: Retirement is the long afternoon after the working day of a life.
normalIntro.cn: retirement 就是一生工作日之后的漫长午后。

normal.en: Early retirement means leaving work before the usual age.
normal.cn: early retirement 意为在通常年龄之前离开工作。

normal.en: Retirement age is the age when people usually stop.
normal.cn: retirement age 是人们通常停止工作的年龄。

normal.en: A retirement plan prepares the money for later.
normal.cn: retirement plan 为以后准备钱。

normal.en: Enjoy one's retirement means live well after work.
normal.cn: enjoy one's retirement 意为退休后过得好。

normal.en: Compare resignation: resignation can happen at any age, retirement usually comes with age.
normal.cn: 对比 resignation：辞职可在任何年龄，退休通常与年龄相关。

abstract.en: Picture a desk cleared of papers for the last time.
abstract.cn: 想象最后一次清空文件的办公桌。

abstract.en: Imagine a clock whose hands move more slowly.
abstract.cn: 想象指针走得更慢的钟。

abstract.en: Think of a garden that finally gets all your mornings.
abstract.cn: 想象一座终于拥有你所有早晨的花园。

examples.en: She is saving for retirement.
examples.cn: 她正在为退休存钱。

examples.en: His retirement party was held in the garden.
examples.cn: 他的退休聚会在花园里举行。

examples.en: The champion announced his retirement at thirty.
examples.cn: 这位冠军在三十岁时宣布退役。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「retire（退休）＋ ment」——退下来之后长久的生活状态，就是退休；这只是构词联想，与词源无关。

root: 法语 retirer（退回）→ retire（退休）＋ -ment → retirement，核心义「从工作中退出后的长久状态」。

sensesIntro.en: Retirement first names the act of leaving work, then the life that follows, and finally the end of a sports career.
sensesIntro.cn: retirement 先指离开工作的行为，再指随后的生活，最后指运动生涯的结束。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a cleared desk and a slow afternoon outside the window.
core.cn: 核心意象：清空的办公桌与窗外缓慢的午后。

branches.en: Leaving work is the core act.
branches.cn: 离开工作是核心行为。

branches.en: The years after work are a new stage.
branches.cn: 工作之后的岁月是新阶段。

branches.en: Athletes retire from competition too.
branches.cn: 运动员也会从比赛中退役。

branches.en: The act opens the long period of freedom.
branches.cn: 这一行为开启了漫长的自由时期。

branches.en: Both jobs and sports careers can end this way.
branches.cn: 工作与运动生涯都能以这种方式结束。

intro.en: Retirement adds the noun suffix -ment to retire.
intro.cn: retirement 在 retire 后加名词后缀 -ment。

latinIntro.en: The word comes through French retirer, to draw back.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词经法语 retirer（退回）传入英语。

items.example: Retired describes a person who left work.
items.exampleCN: retired 描述离开工作的人。

definition_zh: 客户；委托人；客户端
definition_en: a person or company that pays for goods or services, a person who uses a professional service, or a computer that requests data from a server
core_image: 会客室里等着谈生意的那位老主顾
scene: 律师事务所的沙发上坐着一位等了很久的先生。 The lawyer met her client at nine in the morning.
sceneCN: 这里 client 指「委托人」（第 2 个义项：接受专业人士服务的人）；句意是律师早上九点会见了她的委托人。

senses.title: A paying customer
senses.definition: a person or company that buys goods or services from a business
senses.definitionCN: 向商家购买商品或服务的个人或公司
senses.example: The firm lost its biggest client last year.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司去年失去了最大的客户。
senses.why: A client is someone who leans on a business for what he needs, so the word suits a steady business relationship.
senses.whyCN: 客户是依靠商家获得所需之物的人，所以这个词适合表示稳定的商业关系。

senses.title: A user of professional services
senses.definition: a person who pays a lawyer, designer or other professional for advice or work
senses.definitionCN: 付钱请律师、设计师等专业人士提供意见或工作的人
senses.example: The architect showed the client three designs.
senses.exampleCN: 建筑师给委托人看了三份设计。
senses.why: Professionals serve one named person rather than a crowd, and that person is called a client.
senses.whyCN: 专业人士服务的是一位具名的人而不是人群，这个人就叫委托人。

senses.title: A computer that requests data
senses.definition: a computer or program that asks a server for data or services
senses.definitionCN: 向服务器请求数据或服务的计算机或程序
senses.example: The client sends a request and waits for the reply.
senses.exampleCN: 客户端发出请求，然后等待回复。
senses.why: Computing borrowed the word because the small machine also depends on a larger provider.
senses.whyCN: 计算机领域借用这个词，因为小机器同样依赖更大的服务方。

intro.en: Client comes from a Latin verb meaning to lean, not from any word for money.
intro.cn: client 出自拉丁语中表示倚靠的动词，与金钱毫无关系。

items.en: The family of clinare described leaning or bending.
items.cn: clinare 这一词族表示倾斜或倚靠。

items.en: Cliens named a follower who leaned on a patron for protection.
items.cn: cliens 指依靠庇护者保护的随从。

items.en: The word passed through French into legal language.
items.cn: 这个词经法语进入法律用语。

items.en: Client first meant a person under another man's protection.
items.cn: client 最初指受他人保护的人。

items.en: Commerce widened it to any paying customer, and computing added the client machine.
items.cn: 商业把它扩展为任何付钱的顾客，计算机又添上客户端之义。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words that echo the spelling of client, while the meaning group names people who buy or use services.
note.cn: 形近组收的是拼写与 client 相近的词，近义组列出购买或使用服务的人。

entries.definition: a place where people go for medical advice or treatment
entries.definitionCN: 人们去看病或咨询的诊所

entries.definition: all the clients of a business or a professional person
entries.definitionCN: 一家企业或一位专业人士的全部客户

entries.definition: to hold on to something tightly
entries.definitionCN: 紧紧抓住某物

entries.definition: a person who buys goods or services from a shop
entries.definitionCN: 在商店购买商品或服务的人

entries.definition: a person who buys and uses goods and services
entries.definitionCN: 购买并使用商品和服务的人

entries.definition: a person who regularly uses a shop, hotel or theatre
entries.definitionCN: 经常光顾某商店、旅馆或剧院的人

normalIntro.en: These hooks work from the leaning root, the waiting room and the difference between a client and a customer.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从倚靠词根、会客室以及客户与顾客的区别入手。

normal.en: Client and customer both buy, but a client usually buys advice or a service.
normal.cn: client 与 customer 都买东西，但 client 通常买的是建议或服务。

normal.en: The Latin cliens was a follower who leaned on a patron.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 cliens 是依靠庇护者的随从。

normal.en: A lawyer has clients, while a supermarket has customers.
normal.cn: 律师有委托人，超市有顾客。

normal.en: The noun clientele keeps the same stem and means the whole group of clients.
normal.cn: 名词 clientele 词干相同，指全部客户。

normal.en: In computing the client asks and the server answers.
normal.cn: 在计算机里，客户端发问，服务器作答。

abstract.en: Picture a man in a coat waiting on a leather sofa with a folder on his knee.
abstract.cn: 想象一位穿外套的先生坐在皮沙发上，膝上放着文件夹。

abstract.en: Picture two hands, one leaning on the other for support.
abstract.cn: 想象两只手，一只手倚着另一只手支撑自己。

abstract.en: Picture a small laptop asking a huge grey server for a file.
abstract.cn: 想象一台小笔记本向巨大的灰色服务器索取文件。

examples.en: The designer sent the client a revised plan.
examples.cn: 设计师把修改后的方案发给了委托人。

examples.en: This bank treats every client as a long-term partner.
examples.cn: 这家银行把每位客户都当作长期伙伴。

examples.en: The client software updates itself once a week.
examples.cn: 客户端软件每周自动更新一次。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 client 想成「倚靠」你的人：他倚赖你的服务，你倚赖他的订单。

root: 源自拉丁语 cliens（依附者），出自表示倾斜、倚靠的词族，本义是依靠庇护者的人。

sensesIntro.en: From a dependent follower to a paying customer, then to the machine that asks a server.
sensesIntro.cn: 从依附的随从，到付钱的客户，再到向服务器发请求的机器。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person leaning on a stronger partner for support.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人倚靠着更强的一方获取支撑。

branches.en: A steady buyer leans on a business, and the business keeps him.
branches.cn: 稳定的买家倚赖商家，商家也留住他。

branches.en: Professional work creates a named person who pays for advice.
branches.cn: 专业工作产生了一位为意见付费的具名之人。

branches.en: Software copies the pattern: the small side asks, the big side answers.
branches.cn: 软件复制了这个模式：小的一方发问，大的一方作答。

branches.en: Both senses keep one idea, a person served rather than a crowd.
branches.cn: 两个义项共有一个意思：被服务的是个人而非人群。

branches.en: Both use the word for the dependent side of a relationship.
branches.cn: 两者都用这个词指关系中的依赖方。

intro.en: The stem client carries the family, and most relatives simply add a suffix or join another word.
intro.cn: 词干 client 撑起整个家族，多数亲属词只是加后缀或与另一词复合。

latinIntro.en: The base is Latin cliens, the dependent follower who leaned on a patron.
latinIntro.cn: 词基是拉丁语 cliens，即倚靠庇护者的依附者。

items.meaning: more than one customer or dependent person
items.example: The studio serves clients in three cities.
items.exampleCN: 这家工作室为三个城市的客户服务。

items.meaning: the whole group of clients of a business
items.example: The cafe has a young clientele.
items.exampleCN: 这家咖啡馆的顾客以年轻人为主。

items.example: The new office opened clientless but hopeful.
items.exampleCN: 新办公室开业时没有客户，却满怀希望。

items.meaning: using one machine to ask and another to answer
items.example: The system follows a client-server model.
items.exampleCN: 该系统采用客户服务器模式。

items.meaning: all the customers a business can rely on
items.example: The merger doubled the client base.
items.exampleCN: 合并使客户基础扩大了一倍。

items.example: She moved into a client-facing role.
items.exampleCN: 她转到了一线面对客户的岗位。

items.example: The team keeps a client-focused habit.
items.exampleCN: 这个团队保持着以客户为中心的习惯。

items.meaning: the state of being a client
items.exampleCN: 客户身份带来定期的报告。

latinEntries.meaning: a follower who depends on a patron
latinEntries.example: Cliens gave English the word client.
latinEntries.exampleCN: cliens 给英语带来了 client 一词。

latinEntries.example: Clinare stands behind the image of leaning.
latinEntries.exampleCN: clinare 是「倚靠」这一意象的来源。

definition_zh: 怀疑；猜疑；疑心
definition_en: a feeling that someone may be guilty or something may be wrong
core_image: 一个人站在门口，透过半开的门缝向里张望
scene: 他的解释引起了老师的怀疑。 His explanation aroused the teacher's suspicion.
sceneCN: 这里 suspicion 是「怀疑」（第 1 个义项）；句意：他的解释引起了老师的怀疑。

senses.title: A feeling of doubt
senses.definition: a feeling that something is wrong or someone is guilty
senses.definitionCN: 觉得某事不对或某人有罪的感觉
senses.example: His explanation aroused the teacher's suspicion.
senses.exampleCN: 他的解释引起了老师的怀疑。
senses.why: This is the core feeling sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是核心的情绪义项。

senses.title: A very small amount
senses.definition: a slight amount of something
senses.definitionCN: 极少的一点
senses.example: There was a suspicion of a smile on her face.
senses.exampleCN: 她脸上有一丝笑意。
senses.why: This sense uses doubt as a measure of a tiny amount.
senses.whyCN: 这一义项用「疑」来衡量极少的一点。

intro.en: Suspicion is the noun form of the Latin verb for mistrusting.
intro.cn: suspicion 是拉丁语「怀疑」动词的名词形式。

items.en: Suspicere meant to mistrust.
items.cn: suspicere 意为怀疑。

items.en: Suspicio meant mistrust.
items.cn: suspicio 意为猜疑。

items.en: Suspicion meant a feeling of doubt.
items.cn: suspicion 意为怀疑之感。

items.en: Suspicion named the state of doubting.
items.cn: suspicion 指怀疑的状态。

items.en: Suspicion also means a very small amount.
items.cn: suspicion 也表示极少的一点。

note.en: Suspicion is compared with look-alike words and with words for doubt.
note.cn: 把 suspicion 与形近词以及表示怀疑的词作比较。

entries.definition: causing doubt
entries.definitionCN: 可疑的

entries.definition: to doubt someone
entries.definitionCN: 怀疑

entries.definition: to stop temporarily
entries.definitionCN: 暂停

entries.definition: uncertainty
entries.definitionCN: 怀疑

entries.definition: lack of trust
entries.definitionCN: 不信任

entries.definition: suspicion of someone
entries.definitionCN: 猜疑

normalIntro.en: Suspicion is doubt with a direction: toward a person or a story.
normalIntro.cn: suspicion 是有方向的怀疑：指向某个人或某个说法。

normal.en: His explanation aroused the teacher's suspicion.
normal.cn: 他的解释引起了老师的怀疑。

normal.en: The man was under suspicion for weeks.
normal.cn: 那个人受到怀疑达数周之久。

normal.en: She looked at the letter with suspicion.
normal.cn: 她带着怀疑看着那封信。

normal.en: There was a suspicion of a smile on her face.
normal.cn: 她脸上有一丝笑意。

normal.en: The evidence cast suspicion on the guard.
normal.cn: 证据把怀疑指向了守卫。

abstract.en: Suspicion is a shadow cast by a hidden possibility.
abstract.cn: 怀疑是隐藏可能性投下的影子。

abstract.en: It protects and it isolates at the same time.
abstract.cn: 它既保护人，也孤立人。

abstract.en: A suspicion can grow from a word into a wall.
abstract.cn: 怀疑可以从一句话长成一堵墙。

examples.en: His explanation aroused the teacher's suspicion.
examples.cn: 他的解释引起了老师的怀疑。

examples.en: The man was under suspicion for weeks.
examples.cn: 那个人受到怀疑达数周之久。

examples.en: There was a suspicion of a smile on her face.
examples.cn: 她脸上有一丝笑意。

dict_mnemonic.note: 词源记忆 · 暗中打量
dict_mnemonic.text: suspicion 与 suspect 同源，核心是暗中打量、心生疑虑，后也引申为「一丝、少许」。

root: 源自拉丁语 suspicio，与 suspicere（怀疑）同源，经古法语进入英语，核心是对他人或事物的疑虑。

sensesIntro.en: Suspicion means a feeling of doubt, or a very small amount of something.
sensesIntro.cn: suspicion 指怀疑之感，也表示极少的一点。

core.en: Doubt aimed at someone or something.
core.cn: 指向某人或某物的怀疑。

branches.en: His explanation aroused the teacher's suspicion.
branches.cn: 他的解释引起了老师的怀疑。

branches.en: She looked at the letter with suspicion.
branches.cn: 她带着怀疑看着那封信。

branches.en: There was a suspicion of a smile on her face.
branches.cn: 她脸上有一丝笑意。

branches.en: A feeling of doubt and a trace of something share one word.
branches.cn: 怀疑之感与一丝痕迹共用一个词。

branches.en: The evidence cast suspicion on the guard.
branches.cn: 证据把怀疑指向了守卫。

intro.en: Suspicion forms suspicions, suspect, and suspicious.
intro.cn: suspicion 可构成复数 suspicions，并与 suspect、suspicious 相关。

latinIntro.en: The Latin specere, to look, is the root behind the whole family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 specere（看）是这一词族的共同词根。

latinEntries.example: Suspicere is the root of suspicion.
latinEntries.exampleCN: suspicere 是 suspicion 的词根。

definition_zh: 使命；任务；（派往国外的）代表团；传教工作；飞行或军事任务
definition_en: a task that a person or group is sent to carry out, or the purpose an organization sets for itself
core_image: 一个人把封好的信交到另一个人手里，那人转身就上路
scene: 山里的诊所缺药，一支小队带着箱子走了两天，把药送到村口就返回。 The team's mission was to reach the village before the rains.
sceneCN: 这里 mission 指被派出去要完成的一项具体任务（第 1 个义项：受派执行的任务）；句意：这支小队的任务是赶在雨季前抵达那个村子。图中可辨识物件：药箱、山路、封好的指令、雨云；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 使命；任务；代表团；传教；飞行任务

senses.title: An organization's declared purpose
senses.titleCN: 一个组织公开宣告的宗旨
senses.definition: the purpose that an organization states as its reason for existing
senses.definitionCN: 一个组织声明为其存在理由的宗旨
senses.example: The mission on the clinic wall is one sentence long.
senses.exampleCN: 诊所墙上的宗旨只有一句话。
senses.why: A body that is sent must know what it was sent for, so the word came to mean a declared purpose.
senses.whyCN: 被派出去的团体必须知道自己为何被派，这个词于是也指公开宣告的宗旨。

senses.title: A journey with a set purpose
senses.titleCN: 带有明确目的的一次出行
senses.definition: a journey or trip undertaken to carry out a particular task
senses.definitionCN: 为完成某项特定任务而进行的行程
senses.example: The supply mission took two days over the pass.
senses.exampleCN: 那次补给任务翻过山口用了两天。
senses.why: The oldest sense is a sending: someone is dispatched, and the going is the task.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的意思是「被派出」：有人被派遣出去，走这一趟就是任务。

senses.title: A group sent abroad
senses.definition: a group of officials sent to another country to represent their government
senses.definitionCN: 被派往他国代表本国政府的官员团体
senses.example: The trade mission met three buyers in one week.
senses.exampleCN: 贸易代表团一周内见了三位买家。
senses.why: When the sending is diplomatic, the word names the people who were sent rather than the errand.
senses.whyCN: 当派遣是外交性质时，这个词指被派出去的人，而不是那件差事。

senses.title: Religious work or a station
senses.definition: the work of spreading a faith, or the settlement where that work is based
senses.definitionCN: 传播信仰的工作，或这项工作所在的驻地
senses.example: The mission ran a school and a small hospital.
senses.exampleCN: 那个传教站办了一所学校和一间小医院。
senses.why: Missionaries were sent, so their posting took the name of the sending.
senses.whyCN: 传教士是被派出去的，因此他们的驻地沿用了「派遣」这个名字。

senses.title: A military operation with an objective
senses.titleCN: 有明确目标的军事行动
senses.definition: a single operation with a stated objective, often by aircraft
senses.definitionCN: 一次有既定目标的行动，常指飞机出动
senses.example: The squadron flew nine missions in a month.
senses.exampleCN: 这个中队一个月里飞了九次任务。
senses.why: An aircrew is sent out with an objective, and the flight becomes the mission.
senses.whyCN: 机组带着目标被派出，这次飞行就成了 mission。

senses.title: A personal calling
senses.definition: the duty that a person feels bound to fulfil in life
senses.definitionCN: 一个人觉得自己一生必须完成的职责
senses.example: Her mission was to teach girls in villages to read.
senses.exampleCN: 她的使命是教村里的女孩识字。
senses.why: A sending can come from inside rather than from a sender, and the word then means a calling.
senses.whyCN: 派遣也可以来自内心而不是来自派遣者，这个词于是指一种召唤。

senses.title: An embassy or delegation office
senses.titleCN: 使馆或代表处的办公机构
senses.definition: the office or building of a country's representative abroad
senses.definitionCN: 一国驻外代表所在的办公机构或馆舍
senses.example: The visa section is on the second floor of the mission.
senses.exampleCN: 签证处在代表处的二楼。
senses.why: The people sent need a place to work, and the building takes the name of the group.
senses.whyCN: 被派出去的人需要一个办公的地方，馆舍便沿用了这群人的名称。

senses.title: A task given to one person
senses.titleCN: 交给某一个人的具体差事
senses.definition: a particular errand or job assigned to an individual
senses.definitionCN: 分配给某一个人的具体差事
senses.example: His mission for the afternoon was to find the missing file.
senses.exampleCN: 他下午的差事是把那份不见的档案找出来。
senses.why: The word scales down to one person and one errand, keeping the same shape of being sent.
senses.whyCN: 这个词能缩小到一个人、一件差事，仍然保持「被派出」的形状。

intro.en: Mission comes from Latin missio 'a sending', built on mittere 'to send'. English first used it for the sending of envoys and missionaries, and later for any task someone is sent to do.
intro.cn: mission 来自拉丁 missio「派遣」，由 mittere「发送」构成。英语最初用它指派遣使节与传教士，后来才指任何被派去完成的任务。

items.en: Latin mittere 'to send, let go' is well recorded, but its deeper origin is uncertain and no older root can be stated with confidence.
items.cn: 拉丁 mittere「发送、放出」记录充分，但其更早来源不确定，无法有把握地给出更古老的词根。

items.en: The past participle missus 'sent' supplies the miss- inside mission, missionary and missile.
items.cn: 过去分词 missus「被送出的」提供了 mission、missionary 与 missile 里的 miss-。

items.en: Missio meant a sending or a letting go; in military Latin it could also mean a discharge from service.
items.cn: missio 意为派遣或放行；在军事拉丁语里也可指解除兵役。

items.en: English took mission in the sixteenth century, first for the sending of envoys, then for the sending of missionaries.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪借入 mission，先指派遣使节，再指派遣传教士。

items.en: By the seventeenth century a mission could be the station itself, and by the eighteenth a permanent embassy.
items.cn: 到十七世纪，mission 可指传教站本身；到十八世纪，又可指常设使馆。

items.en: Aviation, space flight and management gave the word its operation and purpose senses in the twentieth century.
items.cn: 航空、航天与管理在二十世纪赋予这个词「行动」与「宗旨」两义。

note.en: The first group shares the miss- root; the second group names other tasks and purposes.
note.cn: 第一组共享 miss- 词根；第二组是其他任务与宗旨的说法。

entries.definition: From missus 'sent', but it names a weapon that is thrown or fired, not a task.
entries.definitionCN: 出自 missus「被送出的」，但指被投出或发射的武器，不是任务。

entries.definition: From dis- 'away' plus mittere 'send', meaning to send away or let go.
entries.definitionCN: 由 dis-「离开」加 mittere「发送」构成，意为打发走、解散。

entries.definition: From trans- 'across' plus mittere, meaning to send across.
entries.definitionCN: 由 trans-「越过」加 mittere 构成，意为发送过去。

entries.definition: From com- 'together' plus mittere, meaning to entrust a task or the body entrusted with it.
entries.definitionCN: 由 com-「共同」加 mittere 构成，意为委托任务，或指受托的机构。

entries.definition: A piece of work to be done, with no idea of being sent.
entries.definitionCN: 一件要做的工作，不含「被派出」之意。

entries.definition: Work given to a person by someone in authority; it stresses the giving.
entries.definitionCN: 由有权者交给某人的工作，强调交付。

entries.definition: The aim behind an action, which is the first sense of mission within an organization.
entries.definitionCN: 行动背后的目标，正是 mission 在组织内部的第一义。

entries.definition: A group sent with authority to represent others, close to the diplomatic sense.
entries.definitionCN: 受权代表他人而被派出的团体，接近外交义。

entries.definition: A strong sense of being called to a kind of work, close to the personal sense.
entries.definitionCN: 强烈感到被召唤去做某类工作，接近个人天职义。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Latin verb, the real family and the real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的拉丁动词、真实的同族词与真实的固定说法。

normal.en: Mittere is to send, and missio is a sending, so a mission is literally something sent.
normal.cn: mittere 是发送，missio 是派遣，因此 mission 字面上就是「被派出的事」。

normal.en: The family runs mission, missionary, missile, dismiss and transmit.
normal.cn: 同族词有 missionary、missile、dismiss 与 transmit。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark it: mission statement, rescue mission, space mission.
normal.cn: 固定说法标出它的用法：使命宣言、救援任务、太空飞行任务。

normal.en: The same word scales from a whole organisation's purpose down to one afternoon errand.
normal.cn: 同一个词能从整个组织的宗旨缩小到一个下午的差事。

normal.en: A sending needs a sender, a message and a road, which is the whole picture.
normal.cn: 一次派遣需要派遣者、消息与一条路，这就是整幅画面。

abstract.en: Picture a sealed letter handed over and a traveller turning at once.
abstract.cn: 想象一封封好的信被交出，旅人当场转身。

abstract.en: Picture a box carried two days over a pass, never set down.
abstract.cn: 想象一只箱子翻过山口走了两天，始终没有放下。

abstract.en: Picture a lamp left burning at a station for those still on the road.
abstract.cn: 想象传教站里为还在路上的人留着一盏灯。

examples.en: The agency rewrote its mission after the flood.
examples.cn: 洪水之后，这个机构重写了它的宗旨。

examples.en: A medical mission reached the island on the third day.
examples.cn: 一支医疗队第三天抵达了这座岛。

examples.en: Her mission for the morning was to find the missing key.
examples.cn: 她上午的差事是找到那把不见了的钥匙。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「miss（送出）+ ion（名词）」——被送出去要做的事，就是任务

root: 拉丁 mittere「发送」→ 过去分词 missus「被送出的」→ missio「派遣」→ 英语 mission。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all begin with a sending: an organization's declared purpose, a purposeful journey, a group sent abroad, a mission station, a military sortie, a personal calling, an embassy office and one person's errand.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都从一次派遣开始：组织宣告的宗旨、有目的的出行、派往国外的团体、传教站、军事出动、个人天职、使馆馆舍，以及一个人的差事。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sealed letter handed over, and a traveller who turns and leaves at once.
core.cn: 核心意象：一封封好的信被交出，旅人转身立刻出发。

branches.en: WHY AND BY WHOM: a declared purpose, and a calling that feels like a sender inside.
branches.cn: 为何与由谁：公开宣告的宗旨，以及像内心派遣者一样的召唤。

branches.en: THE GOING ITSELF: a purposeful trip, and a sortie with a stated objective.
branches.cn: 出行本身：一趟有目的的行程，以及一次有既定目标的出动。

branches.en: THE PEOPLE AND THEIR ROOM: a delegation abroad, and the building it works in.
branches.cn: 人与他们的房间：驻外代表团，以及它办公的馆舍。

branches.en: THE STATION: missionaries were sent, so their posting took the name of the sending.
branches.cn: 驻地：传教士被派出，因此驻地沿用了「派遣」之名。

branches.en: ONE ERRAND: the whole picture shrinks to a single afternoon's task.
branches.cn: 一件差事：整幅画面缩小到一个下午的任务。

intro.en: Mission is a Latin participle and action noun from the verb 'to send', and the same verb reaches several common English words.
intro.cn: mission 是由「发送」动词来的拉丁分词与动作名词，同一个动词还通向若干常用英语词。

latinIntro.en: Latin mittere gives mission, missile, dismiss, transmit and commission.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 mittere 衍生 mission、missile（导弹）、dismiss（打发走）、transmit（传送）与 commission（委托）。

items.example: The root supplies the act of sending.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根提供「发送」这个动作。

items.example: The participle supplies the miss- of the family.
items.exampleCN: 这个分词提供词族里的 miss-。

items.example: The action noun is the direct source of mission.
items.exampleCN: 这个动作名词是 mission 的直接来源。

items.meaning: a task one is sent to do
items.example: The English word widened from sending to errand.
items.exampleCN: 英语词从「派遣」扩到「差事」。

items.meaning: one sent to spread a faith
items.example: The suffix marks the person sent.
The same root sends a weapon instead of a person.
items.exampleCN: 同一词根送出的是武器而不是人。

items.example: The prefix reverses the direction of sending.
items.exampleCN: 前缀把发送的方向反过来。

items.example: The prefix lengthens the road of the sending.
Entrusting is sending a task with authority.
items.exampleCN: 委托就是带着权力把任务送出去。

definition_zh: 救护车；急救人员；流动医院；急救转运服务
definition_en: a vehicle, aircraft or boat specially equipped to carry sick or injured people, or the medical service that operates it
core_image: 一辆车灯闪动的白色车，把伤者从出事地点送往能救人的地方
scene: 雨夜的十字路口，一辆自行车倒在地上，路人围成一圈。 An ambulance arrived within four minutes and took the rider to hospital.
sceneCN: 这里 ambulance 是「救护车」（第 1 个义项：运送伤病者的专用车辆）；句意为四分钟内来了一辆救护车，把骑车人送到医院。画面里有雨夜路口、倒地的自行车与闪灯的车。

pos.zh: 名词：救护车；急救人员；流动医院；急救转运服务

collocations.zh: 救护车服务；急救转运服务
空中救护飞机或直升机

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁语「行走」分词词干加 -ant 构成，义为「走动的；能行走的」，用于医学与正式语境
由拉丁语 ambulare 加 -ory 构成，义为「可走动的；与行走有关的」
由拉丁语 ambulare 借入的动词，义为「行走」，多用于医学描述

senses.title: A vehicle for the sick or injured
senses.definition: a road vehicle equipped with medical supplies and stretchers to take sick or injured people to hospital
senses.definitionCN: 装有医疗用品与担架、用于把伤病者送往医院的陆上车辆
senses.example: An ambulance took the cyclist to hospital with a broken arm.
senses.exampleCN: 一辆救护车把手臂骨折的骑车人送到了医院。
senses.why: The French name first described a walking hospital; once the hospital was mounted on wheels, the vehicle inherited the name.
senses.whyCN: 法语原名本指「会走动的医院」；当这座医院被装上轮子，名字就落到了车上。

senses.title: A specially equipped aircraft or boat
senses.definition: an aircraft or vessel fitted with medical equipment for moving patients, especially over long or difficult distances
senses.definitionCN: 装有医疗设备、用于长距离或难走路线转运病人的飞机或船只
senses.example: An air ambulance flew the injured climber to the city.
senses.exampleCN: 一架空中救护飞机把受伤的登山者送到了城里。
senses.why: The core idea is a moving treatment room, so any carrier that can hold one qualifies.
senses.whyCN: 核心观念是「会移动的救治室」，因此任何能装下它的载具都符合条件。

senses.title: A mobile field hospital
senses.definition: the older sense of a hospital unit that moved with an army close to the fighting
senses.definitionCN: 较古老的义项：随军队移动、靠近战场的医院单位
senses.example: During the war, the ambulance moved closer to the front every week.
senses.exampleCN: 战争期间，这座流动医院每周都向更靠近前线的地方移动。
senses.why: This is the original French sense: the hospital itself walked, not the vehicle that later carried patients.
senses.whyCN: 这是法语本义：会「走」的是医院本身，而不是后来运送病人的车辆。

senses.title: The crew who staff the vehicle
senses.definition: by metonymy, the paramedics and medical team travelling in the vehicle
senses.definitionCN: 借代用法，指随车出动的急救人员与医疗小组
senses.example: The ambulance was already treating the driver when we arrived.
senses.exampleCN: 我们赶到时，救护人员已经在给司机做处理了。
senses.why: The vehicle and its crew always arrive together, so the name of the container stands for the people inside.
senses.whyCN: 车与人总是一起到场，于是容器的名字就代指里面的人。

senses.title: The emergency transport service
senses.definition: the organized service that provides emergency transport and pre-hospital care
senses.definitionCN: 提供紧急转运与院前急救的有组织服务体系
senses.example: The island depends on a volunteer ambulance that runs around the clock.
senses.exampleCN: 这座岛依赖一支全天候运转的志愿急救转运队伍。
senses.why: Beyond one vehicle, the word can name the whole arrangement that keeps such vehicles moving.
senses.whyCN: 超过单辆车之后，这个词也能指让这些车持续运转的整套安排。

intro.en: Ambulance is a French military-medical coinage built on a Latin verb for walking.
intro.cn: ambulance 是法语里由军事医疗需要造出的词，底层是一个表示「行走」的拉丁动词。

items.en: The verb ambulare meant 'to walk, to go about'. It is the walking root behind the whole family.
items.cn: 动词 ambulare 意为「行走、走动」，是整个词族背后的「行走」词根。

items.en: French military medicine spoke of a hôpital ambulant, literally a walking hospital that followed the troops.
items.cn: 法国军队医疗中出现了 hôpital ambulant 的说法，字面是「会走动的医院」，随部队移动。

items.en: The phrase was shortened to ambulance, which named the mobile medical unit itself.
items.cn: 这一短语被缩略为 ambulance，用来指流动医疗单位本身。

items.en: English adopted the word in the nineteenth century, and its use spread widely in the Crimean War period. The exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 英语在十九世纪借入这个词，并在克里米亚战争时期广泛使用；确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: Motor ambulances fixed the word to a road vehicle, while air ambulance extended it to aircraft.
items.cn: 机动救护车把词义固定在陆上车辆上，空中救护又把范围扩到飞机。

note.en: The look-alike group is the walking family from Latin ambulare; the near-meaning group gathers the people and equipment of emergency care.
note.cn: 形近组收由拉丁语 ambulare「行走」衍生的一族词；近义组收急救场景中的人员与设备。

entries.definition: Adjective: able to walk, or relating to walking; also used for outpatient care.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「能走动的、与行走有关的」，也用于「门诊的」这一医疗说法。

entries.definition: Adjective: walking or able to walk; a formal medical word.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「走动的、能行走的」，属正式医学用词。

entries.definition: Verb: to walk, especially in medical descriptions of a patient.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「行走」，多用于病历中对病人的描述。

entries.definition: A person trained to give emergency medical treatment before a patient reaches hospital.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「急救员」，指在病人入院前提供紧急医疗处理的人。

entries.definition: A frame with a sheet for carrying a sick or injured person.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「担架」，指用来抬送伤病者的框架床。

entries.definition: The act of freeing someone from danger; broader than transport to hospital.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或动词，义为「救援」，指把人从危险中救出，范围比送医更宽。

entries.definition: A sudden serious situation needing immediate action; the condition that calls an ambulance.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「紧急情况」，指需要立即处理的突发严重状况，也是叫救护车的原因。

normalIntro.en: These hooks trace the real Latin walking verb and the French military hospital behind the word.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子沿着真实的拉丁「行走」动词，以及这个词背后的法国军医院展开。

normal.en: Ambulare is to walk: the first ambulance was a hospital that walked with the army.
normal.cn: ambulare 是「行走」：最早的 ambulance 是一座随军行走的医院。

normal.en: French shortened hôpital ambulant to ambulance; the adjective became the noun.
normal.cn: 法语把 hôpital ambulant 缩成 ambulance，形容词变成了名词。

normal.en: Ambulatory and ambulant keep the walking sense in modern medical English.
normal.cn: ambulatory 与 ambulant 在现代医学英语里保留了「行走」义。

normal.en: Air ambulance extends the same idea to aircraft and helicopters.
normal.cn: air ambulance 把同一观念扩展到飞机与直升机。

normal.en: The crew is called the ambulance by metonymy, because vehicle and team arrive as one.
normal.cn: 急救人员也被称作 ambulance，这是借代，因为车与人是一起到场的。

abstract.en: Picture a small hospital on wheels rolling through mud, its white walls shaking, still treating whoever is inside.
abstract.cn: 想象一座装在小轮子上的医院在泥地里前行，白墙摇晃，仍在救治里面的人。

abstract.en: Picture a bright rectangle moving against a dark street: the light is not the cure, but it is the promise of one.
abstract.cn: 想象暗街上移动的一块亮色：那光不是治疗本身，却是治疗将要到来的承诺。

abstract.en: Picture a door that opens exactly where someone fell, as if the building had walked to the patient.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇门正好在有人倒下的地方打开，仿佛整座建筑走到了病人身边。

examples.en: An ambulance arrived within four minutes and took the rider to hospital.
examples.cn: 四分钟内来了一辆救护车，把骑车人送到了医院。

examples.en: The ambulance crew kept talking to the injured man to keep him calm.
examples.cn: 急救人员不停地和受伤男子说话，让他保持镇定。

examples.en: In remote valleys, an air ambulance is often the only fast way to a surgeon.
examples.cn: 在偏远山谷，空中救护常常是尽快见到外科医生的唯一办法。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「俺不能死」——车里的人一路喊着这句话，车就往医院冲：救护车

root: 拉丁语 ambulare「行走」是词根；法语把随军的 hôpital ambulant（会走动的医院）缩略成 ambulance，先指流动医院，后指运送伤病者的车辆。英语于十九世纪借入，克里米亚战争时期广泛使用；确切首见年代不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses follow one moving treatment room: the road vehicle, the aircraft or boat, the original walking hospital, the crew inside it, and the service that keeps it running.
sensesIntro.cn: 五个义项围绕同一间「会移动的救治室」：陆上车辆、空中或水上载具、最初的流动医院、车里的急救人员，以及让这一切运转的服务体系。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a white room with wheels moves toward the injured and carries them back to safety.
core.cn: 核心意象：一间带轮子的白色房间朝伤者移动，再把他们带回安全处。

branches.en: THE ROAD LINE: the ordinary vehicle that carries patients to hospital.
branches.cn: 道路线：把病人送往医院的普通车辆，是今天最常见的用法。

branches.en: THE AIR AND SEA LINE: the same room fitted into aircraft or boats for long distances.
branches.cn: 空海线：同一间救治室被装进飞机或船只，用于长距离转运。

branches.en: THE ORIGINAL LINE: the hospital itself walked with the army before any vehicle took the name.
branches.cn: 本义线：在任何车辆得名之前，会走的是医院本身，它随军移动。

branches.en: THE PEOPLE LINE: the crew stands for the vehicle by metonymy.
branches.cn: 人员线：急救人员借代车辆，因为两者总是一起到场。

branches.en: THE SYSTEM LINE: one vehicle expands into an organized emergency service.
branches.cn: 体系线：一辆车扩展成有组织的急救服务体系。

intro.en: Ambulance joins a Latin walking stem to a French noun suffix, and later English adds combining words for motor and air versions.
intro.cn: ambulance 把拉丁语「行走」词干与法语名词后缀接在一起，后来英语又加入 motor 与 air 这类组合成分。

latinIntro.en: Latin ambulare and its participles are recorded; the French shortened form is also documented, so nothing here is reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 ambulare 及其分词形式都有记录，法语缩略形式也有文献可查，因此这里没有重构形式。

items.exampleCN: 它是这一词族的「行走」核心。

items.example: The verb is the source of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是整个词族的来源。

items.example: The participle describes the hospital that moves.
items.exampleCN: 这个分词描述「会移动的」医院。

items.example: French gave the shortened noun its military sense.

items.exampleCN: 它把「行走」词干变成名词。

definition_zh: 自然地；天生地；理所当然地；未经人工干预地；不做作地
definition_en: in a natural way, by nature, or as one would reasonably expect
core_image: 一粒种子落在土里，没有支架，也没有指令，它自己朝光长出一片叶子。
scene: 朋友听说你刚搬到海边，笑着说，这大概会自然而然发生。 Living by the sea, you will naturally start swimming every day.
sceneCN: 这里 naturally 是“理所当然地、自然而然”（第 3 个义项）；句意：住在海边，你自然会开始每天游泳；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 自然地；天生地；理所当然地；未经人工干预地；不做作地

collocations.zh: 生来就会；做起来很自然

senses.title: In nature's own way
senses.titleCN: 以自然的方式：不按人为规矩来
senses.definition: in a way that follows nature rather than human design or convention
senses.definitionCN: 依照自然而非人为设计或惯例的方式进行
senses.example: The river runs naturally through the valley, without any concrete banks.
senses.exampleCN: 这条河自然地流过山谷，两岸没有水泥护岸。
senses.why: The adverb describes the manner of an action: it happens as nature would have it, so the absence of human arrangement is the point.
senses.whyCN: 这个副词描述动作的方式：事情按自然本来的样子发生，所以“没有人为安排”正是重点。

senses.title: From birth, by temperament
senses.titleCN: 天生地：生来就带着的本事或性情
senses.definition: as a result of inborn ability or character rather than training
senses.definitionCN: 出于与生俱来的能力或性格，而非后天训练
senses.example: She naturally remembers faces, even ones she has seen only once.
senses.exampleCN: 她天生记得住面孔，哪怕只见过一次。
senses.why: Here the adverb points to the origin of an ability: the talent is treated as part of the person's constitution, not as an acquired skill.
senses.whyCN: 这里副词指向能力的来源：这份才能被视为个人禀赋的一部分，而不是后天习得的技能。

senses.title: As you would expect
senses.titleCN: 理所当然：事情本就该这样
senses.definition: as is reasonable or unsurprising, given the circumstances
senses.definitionCN: 在那种情形下合乎情理、并不令人意外
senses.example: Naturally, the children were excited the night before the trip.
senses.exampleCN: 出发前一晚孩子们很兴奋，这是理所当然的。
senses.why: This sense is about inference, not nature: the speaker says the outcome follows so obviously that no explanation is needed.
senses.whyCN: 这一义项关乎推理而非自然：说话者表示结果显然如此，根本无须解释。

senses.title: Without human help
senses.titleCN: 未经人工干预：自己长出来的
senses.definition: happening or existing without cultivation, manufacture, or intervention
senses.definitionCN: 在没有栽培、制造或人为干预的情况下发生或存在
senses.example: The valley is naturally protected from strong winds by its surrounding hills.
senses.exampleCN: 这个山谷因四周的丘陵而天然不受强风侵袭。
senses.why: The word marks a cause that is not human: whatever produced the result was already there, so no one deserves credit or blame for it.
senses.whyCN: 这个词标出非人为的原因：产生结果的东西本来就存在，因此无人该为此受功或受责。

senses.title: Without pretending
senses.titleCN: 不做作：不摆姿态、不加表演
senses.definition: in a relaxed and sincere manner that shows no affectation
senses.definitionCN: 以放松而真诚的方式，不显出做作
senses.example: On camera she laughed naturally, not the way she laughed in advertisements.
senses.exampleCN: 镜头前她笑得很自然，不是广告里那种笑法。
senses.why: Praise of natural behaviour measures the distance between a person and a performance; the smaller the distance, the more naturally it is done.
senses.whyCN: 称赞举止自然，衡量的是“人”与“表演”之间的距离；距离越小，就做得越自然。

senses.title: By logical consequence
senses.titleCN: 顺理成章：顺着前提必然走到这里
senses.definition: as a necessary or logical consequence of what came before
senses.definitionCN: 作为先前事情必然或合乎逻辑的结果
senses.example: Naturally, a longer delay meant a higher final cost.
senses.exampleCN: 工期拖得更久，最终成本自然更高。
senses.why: The sense borrows the idea of nature as an inevitable order and applies it to reasoning: given the premise, the conclusion could hardly be otherwise.
senses.whyCN: 这一义项借用了“自然是一种必然秩序”的观念，并把它用于推理：前提既定，结论几乎不可能不是这样。

senses.title: Found in the wild
senses.titleCN: 天然存在：自然界里本来就有
senses.definition: occurring in nature rather than being made or introduced by people
senses.definitionCN: 存在于自然界，而非由人制造或引入
senses.example: The element is naturally present in seawater at a very low concentration.
senses.exampleCN: 这种元素天然存在于海水中，浓度极低。
senses.why: In science the word distinguishes a substance that was already in the environment from one released or synthesised by humans.
senses.whyCN: 在科学语境里，这个词区分“本来就在环境中的物质”与“人类释放或合成的物质”。

senses.title: Easily and smoothly
senses.titleCN: 从容自如：做起来不费劲
senses.definition: with ease and fluency, as if no effort were required
senses.definitionCN: 轻松流畅地，仿佛不需要用力
senses.example: After a month of practice, the steps came naturally to him.
senses.exampleCN: 练了一个月后，这些步骤他做起来已从容自如。
senses.why: Skill that has become second nature no longer shows the seams of conscious control; the adverb reports that ease rather than describing the world.
senses.whyCN: 熟练到成为第二天性时，动作不再露出刻意控制的痕迹；这个副词报告的是这种轻松，而不是在描述世界。

intro.en: Naturally is natural plus the adverb suffix -ly. Natural goes back through French to Latin natura and the verb nasci, to be born.
intro.cn: naturally 是 natural 加副词后缀 -ly。natural 经法语上溯至拉丁语 natura 与动词 nasci“出生”。

items.en: Nasci meant to be born or to arise. From it came natura, the condition and character one has at birth.
items.cn: nasci 意为“出生、产生”。由它派生出 natura，指出生时的状况与禀性。

items.en: Naturalis described what belongs to nature or comes from it, as opposed to what art or human skill produces.
items.cn: naturalis 描述属于自然或来自自然的东西，与技艺或人力所产相对。

items.en: Old French naturel kept both senses: the physical world and a person's inborn disposition.
items.cn: 古法语 naturel 保留两层含义：物质世界，以及人的固有性情。

items.en: English formed adverbs with -ly from Old English -lice. Naturally therefore means 'in a natural manner' before it means 'of course'.
items.cn: 英语用 -ly（古英语 -lice）构成副词。因此 naturally 先表示“以自然的方式”，之后才引申出“当然”。

items.en: The 'as expected' sense grew out of the idea that nature follows a fixed order: what is natural is also what regularly happens.
items.cn: “如所预料”义由“自然遵循固定秩序”的观念生长出来：合乎自然的，也就是经常发生的。

items.en: Science writing added naturally occurring; speech and performance writing added the sense of ease without affectation.
items.cn: 科学写作发展出 naturally occurring（天然存在）；言语与表演领域则发展出“从容不做作”的义项。

note.en: The first group shares the nature root; the second compares adverbs that describe how an action comes about.
note.cn: 第一组共享 nature 词根；第二组比较几个描述“动作如何发生”的副词。

entries.definition: existing in nature, inborn, or normal. It modifies a noun.
entries.definitionCN: 自然界存在的、天生的或正常的；修饰名词。

entries.definition: the physical world, or the essential character of something.
entries.definitionCN: 物质世界，或某物的本质特性。

entries.definition: the quality of being natural or free from affectation.
entries.definitionCN: 自然、不做作的性质。

entries.definition: as everyone knows or expects. It marks the obviousness of a fact, not its origin.
entries.definitionCN: 众所周知或如人所料；标出事实的显然，而不涉其来源。

entries.definition: in a way that cannot be avoided. It is stronger than naturally and implies necessity.
entries.definitionCN: 以无法避免的方式；比 naturally 更强，含必然性。

entries.definition: by automatic animal impulse rather than thought. It applies to living creatures.
entries.definitionCN: 凭本能的自动冲动而非思考；适用于生物。

entries.definition: from one's own impulse, without planning; also happening without external cause.
entries.definitionCN: 出于自身冲动、未经计划；也指无外在原因地发生。

normalIntro.en: Real parts only: natural + -ly. The suffix simply turns the adjective into an adverb, so the meaning tracks natural.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分：natural 加 -ly。后缀只是把形容词变成副词，词义随 natural 走。

normal.en: Natural + -ly: do it the way nature would, with no scaffolding.
normal.cn: natural 加 -ly：照自然的方式做，不加支架。

normal.en: A talent you never trained comes naturally; a habit you drilled also comes naturally after enough practice.
normal.cn: 没练过的才能，说起来就是“生来就会”；练够了的习惯，用起来也同样轻松自如。

normal.en: In a chemistry paper, naturally means it was already in the water.
normal.cn: 在化学论文里，naturally 表示它本来就在水里。

normal.en: Naturally at the start of a sentence usually means 'as you can guess'.
normal.cn: naturally 放在句首，通常就是“你猜也猜得到”。

normal.en: A good actor makes a rehearsed line sound naturally spoken.
normal.cn: 好演员能把排练过的台词说得像自然说出的一样。

abstract.en: Nature and reason share one adverb: what always happens and what must follow are felt to be the same order.
abstract.cn: 自然与理性共用一个副词：总会发生的事与必然推出的事，被感受为同一种秩序。

abstract.en: Saying 'naturally' hides who arranged the conditions; it presents a result as if no one had chosen it.
abstract.cn: 说 naturally 会隐藏是谁安排了条件：它把结果呈现得好像无人选择过。

abstract.en: Effortless skill is nature edited by years of practice, and the adverb keeps the editing out of sight.
abstract.cn: 举重若轻的技艺，是被多年练习剪辑过的自然；而这个副词把剪辑痕迹藏在镜头外。

examples.en: The lake is naturally too cold for swimming until late June.
examples.cn: 这个湖天然太冷，要到六月下旬才适合游泳。

examples.en: Naturally, the students who read the whole book did better on the essay question.
examples.cn: 读过整本书的学生在论述题上表现更好，这是理所当然的。

examples.en: She stepped onto the stage and began to speak naturally, as if the audience were old friends.
examples.cn: 她走上台，自然地开口，仿佛观众都是老朋友。

dict_mnemonic.text: natural（自然的）+ ly（地）——自然地；事情按常理发展，也就成了“当然”。

root: 由 natural（自然的，源自拉丁语 natura“出生、本性”，出自 nasci“出生”）加副词后缀 -ly 构成，本义为“以自然的方式”，后引申为“天生地、理所当然地”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of naturally. One thread runs through them: something happens without visible human arrangement. That can mean without cultivation, without training, without affectation, or simply without any need to explain.
sensesIntro.cn: naturally 的八个义项由一条线串起：事情发生，却看不出人为安排。这可以指未经栽培、未经训练、不加做作，或干脆无须解释。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a seed in bare soil, growing toward the light with no stake and no instruction.
core.cn: 核心意象：裸土里的一粒种子，没有支架也没有指令，自己朝光生长。

branches.en: WITHOUT HUMAN DESIGN: a free river and an element already in seawater both exist before anyone acts.
branches.cn: 无人为设计：自由流淌的河与海水中本就存在的元素，都在人行动之前就已存在。

branches.en: WITHOUT TRAINING: inborn memory and practised ease both look as if no learning took place.
branches.cn: 未经训练：天生的记忆力与练成的从容，看起来都像没有学习过。

branches.en: WITHOUT EXPLANATION: 'as you would expect' and 'by consequence' both present the result as obvious.
branches.cn: 无须解释：“如你所料”与“顺理成章”都把结果呈现为显然。

branches.en: WITHOUT CULTIVATION: shelter and protection supplied by terrain rather than by builders.
branches.cn: 未经栽培：由地形而非建造者提供的遮蔽与保护。

branches.en: WITHOUT PERFORMANCE: behaviour that does not advertise itself as behaviour.
branches.cn: 不加表演：举止不把自己标榜为“举止”。

intro.en: Naturally is natural plus -ly, the standard English adverb suffix. The family spreads through -ness, -ism, -ist, -ize, and the prefix un-.
intro.cn: naturally 是 natural 加 -ly，即英语标准副词后缀。词族再通过 -ness、-ism、-ist、-ize 与否定前缀 un- 扩展。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is nasci, to be born, giving natura and naturalis. English -ly descends from Old English -lice, not from Latin.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词基是 nasci“出生”，由此得到 natura 与 naturalis。英语 -ly 则源自古英语 -lice，并非来自拉丁语。

items.meaning: the physical world, or the inborn character of something
items.meaningCN: 自然界；或事物的固有本性
items.example: The nature of the clay decides how the pot will fire.
items.exampleCN: 陶土的性质决定这只陶罐烧成后的样子。

items.meaning: existing in nature, inborn, or normal
items.meaningCN: 自然存在的；天生的；正常的
items.example: The harbour is a natural shelter for small boats.
items.exampleCN: 这个港湾是小船天然的避风处。

items.meaning: in a natural manner; as expected
items.meaningCN: 以自然的方式；如所预料
items.example: The trail climbs naturally along the ridge.
items.exampleCN: 这条小径顺着山脊自然向上延伸。

items.meaning: the quality of being natural or unaffected
items.example: The naturalness of her voice made the recording easy to trust.
items.exampleCN: 她声音里的自然感让这段录音容易让人信服。

items.meaning: the view that nature is all of reality
items.meaningCN: 自然即全部现实的学说
items.example: Naturalism rejects explanations that step outside nature.
items.exampleCN: 自然主义拒绝越出自然之外的解释。

items.meaning: a field researcher of living things
items.meaningCN: 野外研究生物的人；博物学家
items.example: The naturalist noted the first migrants of spring.
items.exampleCN: 这位博物学家记下了春天第一批迁徙的鸟。

items.meaning: to make natural, or to establish a species or word as native
items.meaningCN: 使自然化；使物种或词语归化
items.example: The plant naturalized quickly in the wet soil.
items.exampleCN: 这种植物在湿土中很快归化了。

items.meaning: contrary to nature or to normal feeling
items.example: The brightness of the sky at midnight seemed unnatural.
items.exampleCN: 午夜天空的亮度显得反常。

items.meaningCN: 存在于自然秩序之外的；超自然的
items.example: The story adds a supernatural explanation to a real famine.
items.exampleCN: 这个故事给一场真实的饥荒加上了超自然解释。

definition_zh: 诚实地；说实话
definition_en: in a truthful way, or used to stress a frank opinion
core_image: 一个人直视对方，把难说出口的真话讲出来
scene: 她诚实地回答了所有问题。 She answered all the questions honestly.
sceneCN: 这里 honestly 是「诚实地」（第 1 个义项）；句意：她诚实地回答了所有问题。

senses.title: In a truthful way
senses.definition: in a way that tells the truth
senses.definitionCN: 以说真话的方式
senses.example: She answered all the questions honestly.
senses.exampleCN: 她诚实地回答了所有问题。
senses.why: This is the manner sense of the adverb.
senses.whyCN: 这是副词表示方式的核心义项。

senses.title: To speak frankly
senses.definition: used to introduce a blunt personal view
senses.definitionCN: 用于引出直率的个人看法
senses.example: Honestly, the plan needs more work.
senses.exampleCN: 说实话，这个计划还需要改进。
senses.why: Here the adverb comments on the whole sentence.
senses.whyCN: 这里副词修饰的是整句话。

intro.cn: honestly 是 honest 加上副词后缀 -ly 构成的。

normalIntro.cn: honestly 是 honest 的副词形式：诚实地做或说。

normal.en: She answered all the questions honestly.
normal.cn: 她诚实地回答了所有问题。

normal.en: He honestly believed he was right.
normal.cn: 他真心相信自己是正确的。

normal.en: Honestly, the plan needs more work.

normal.en: They spoke honestly about their fears.

normal.en: Quite honestly, I was surprised.

abstract.en: Honestly is truth wearing everyday clothes.
abstract.cn: honestly 是穿上日常衣服的真相。

abstract.en: To speak honestly is to trust the listener.

abstract.en: A frank word can open a closed room.
abstract.cn: 坦率的话，能打开一间关着的屋子。
